name: Feature-scored engine selection over a declared capability matrix
what: For every scrape the engine list is computed from the request's feature flags (actions, waitFor, screenshot, location, mobile, stealth proxy, branding, file type). Engines that support too little of the request are dropped, the rest are ordered by support score then a fixed quality rank, and any feature the winning engine could not honour is returned as a 'scrape may be partial' warning.
how: engines/index.ts declares 17 feature flags with hand-set priorities (waitFor 1, screenshot 10, actions 20, atsv and useFastMode 90, pdf/document/image/audio/video 100) and a boolean feature matrix per engine plus a quality number (x-twitter 1500, index 1000, wikipedia 500, chrome-cdp 50, retry-cdp 45, playwright 20, tlsclient 10, fetch 5, file parsers -20, stealth variants -2 to -15). buildFallbackList keeps engines whose supported-priority sum is at least floor(total/2), drops negative-quality engines whenever a positive one qualifies, and sorts by supportScore then quality. scrapeURL turns the leftover unsupported flags into document.warning.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's DriverPlan picks a driver from three booleans (actions, screenshot, pdf); a declared capability matrix with weights would let Verevon add Kernel/Browserless/Browserbase drivers and explain every driver choice in receipts.
notes: Quality 4: explainable and extensible, but weights and thresholds are hand-tuned magic numbers and several engines (all stealth/CDP ones) are closed-source so the matrix cannot be fully exercised from this repo.

name: Hedged engine waterfall with sniping of losers
what: Engines are tried in order, but a slow engine does not block the next one: when an engine passes its 'max reasonable time' the next engine starts while the first keeps running, and the first acceptable result wins while the others are aborted. A hard engine error starts the next engine immediately.
how: scrapeURLLoop keeps a list of in-flight engine promises and awaits Promise.race over them plus a timer; the timer (engine max-reasonable-time plus SCRAPEURL_ENGINE_WATERFALL_DELAY_MS, default 0) rejects with WaterfallNextEngineSignal to launch the next engine. When a winner returns, snipeAbortController aborts the rest (EngineSnipedError). Per-engine MRT: index 1.5 s, fetch/document/tlsclient 15 s, playwright waitFor+30 s, chrome-cdp waitFor + summed action time + 30 s. A hard overall cap of 5 minutes applies when no timeout was requested.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's FallbackDriver is strictly sequential (rotate on 401/403/407/429/503 or JS-shell detection); hedging static-to-browser only when the static driver is slow would cut tail latency at the cost of duplicated work, and needs an org budget guard.
notes: Quality 5: tail-latency aware and cancellation-clean. Cost is duplicated engine work (each hedged engine is billed upstream) and the design assumes engines are idempotent reads.

name: Typed re-plan signals with bounded retry budgets
what: An engine can tell the orchestrator to re-plan instead of just failing: 'add feature X' (stealth proxy, pdf, document, image) or 'remove feature Y'. Re-planning re-runs the whole waterfall with new flags, but per-scrape counters cap total attempts (6), feature toggles (3), removals (3) and file prefetches (2) so escalation cannot loop.
how: AddFeatureError and RemoveFeatureError carry feature flags and optional pdf/document/image prefetch payloads. The catch loop in scrapeURL records each re-plan in ScrapeRetryTracker, merges flags via applyHandoffFeatureFlags (a file handoff drops the conflicting extension-implied file flag), and uses a undefined-vs-null prefetch sentinel to tell 'browser never tried' from 'browser ran but delivered no file'. Exceeding a budget throws ScrapeRetryLimitError with the stat snapshot.
verevonRelevance: A small typed escalation vocabulary (NeedsStealth, NeedsBrowser, IsFile{kind}, DropFeature) plus budgets would give Quarry a principled place to put the escalate() logic that SCRAPING_ENGINE_GAPS.md says never fires.
notes: Quality 5: the null/undefined prefetch sentinel and shared antibot+proxy prefetch budget show real bug-driven hardening.

name: Empty-page gate: a 2xx page with no content makes the engine fail, other statuses pass through
what: An engine counts as failed only when it returns a 2xx/304 page whose content converts to empty markdown (checked first with main-content extraction, then without); the waterfall then moves to the next engine. Any non-2xx result (404, 500...) is accepted and returned with its status code, except 401/403/429 under proxy 'auto', which escalates to the stealth proxy instead.
how: scrapeURLLoopIter converts engine HTML via htmlTransform + parseMarkdown (skipped when HTML > 300 KB, in which case raw HTML is checked), computes isLongEnough (despite the name, just non-empty), isGoodStatusCode (2xx or 304) and hasNoPageError (logged only), and accepts when isParsedImage || isLongEnough || !isGoodStatusCode; otherwise it throws EngineUnsuccessfulError. isLikelyProxyError (401/403/429) with proxy 'auto' and no stealth flag throws AddFeatureError(['stealthProxy']) before the decision.
verevonRelevance: Quarry already has soft-404 detection, JS-shell escalation and ChallengeKind classification; the extra idea here is returning non-2xx pages as results (with status) instead of retrying them, and treating only empty 2xx pages as engine failures.
notes: Quality 3: crude. A TODO in the code admits that deciding on bad status codes is hard; a 200 page that is a bot wall or soft 404 with text is accepted, and there is no in-repo captcha or bot-wall text detection (that lives in closed fire-engine plus the LLM-judged engpicker).

name: Open-core split: what the OSS repo really ships as engines
what: The open-source repo ships only a plain fetch engine, a minimal Playwright microservice and PDF/document/image parsers. Real browser rendering with actions, screenshots, geolocation, mobile, stealth, branding, the URL cache and site-specific engines depend on closed services (fire-engine, index DB, Hangar, FirePDF) reached by URL.
how: The engine list is built from config presence checks: x-twitter (XAI key or DB auth), wikipedia (credentials), index/index;documents (INDEX_DATABASE_URL), six fire-engine variants (FIRE_ENGINE_BETA_URL), playwright (PLAYWRIGHT_MICROSERVICE_URL), then fetch, pdf, document and image (only with FIRE_PDF_BASE_URL). The Playwright feature row supports only waitFor and skipTlsVerification. Requesting actions without fire-engine throws ActionsNotSupportedError saying Fire Engine is required. SELF_HOST.md recommends bundled Playwright with fetch fallback and says to connect Fire-engine separately.
verevonRelevance: Parity should be measured against the closed fire-engine contract, not the OSS code: copy request/response shapes and escalation semantics, and expect no anti-bot code to borrow.
notes: Quality 3 for the OSS tier: honest about being a skeleton. The previous Verevon docs describe fire-engine behaviours (HMAC signing, DNS caching) that this repo does not show.

name: Plain HTTP engine with charset detection and cookie jar
what: The fetch engine downloads with undici, follows redirects, decodes bodies using header charset then meta charset then UTF-8, keeps a per-request cookie jar and hands non-HTML file types to the PDF/document/image parsers.
how: scrapeURLWithFetch calls undici.fetch with getSecureDispatcher (SSRF guard, optional ProxyAgent, tough-cookie jar via http-cookie-agent, redirect interceptor with maxRedirections 5000). decodeHtmlBuffer tries TextDecoder(header charset), then meta charset, then utf8, logging decode failures. specialtyScrapeCheck runs on the response headers. Max reasonable time 15 s. A mock layer can record and replay responses.
verevonRelevance: Low: Quarry's StaticDriver already sniffs charsets and pins DNS; the only takeaway is the header-then-meta charset order and fail-soft decoding.
notes: Redirect cap of 5000 is effectively unbounded.

name: TLS-impersonating client tier and its demotion rules
what: fire-engine's tlsclient is a fast, no-JS tier (quality 10, supports atsv anti-bot solver and fast mode) that is deliberately removed from the normal waterfall when fire-engine exists, because falling back to a plain client after Chrome fails tends to return bot-walled content.
how: buildFallbackList splices out fire-engine;tlsclient(+stealth) and fetch when useFireEngine is true unless the request sets useFastMode, atsv, audio or video, or the engpicker verdict for the domain is TlsClientOk (which also boosts its quality by 50). scrapeURLWithFireEngineTLSClient posts engine 'tlsclient' with mobileProxy (stealth) and autoProxy flags and a 15 s max reasonable time.
verevonRelevance: Quarry owns a real TLS-impersonation driver (wreq JA3/JA4/H2, Chrome profile only); Firecrawl's rule 'never degrade from browser to plain client' is a useful counter-policy to Quarry's static-first plan.
notes: The tlsclient internals are in closed fire-engine; only its contract is visible.

name: Playwright microservice: per-request context isolation and bounded pages
what: A separate Express service renders pages in Chromium with a fresh browser context per request (random user agent from the user-agents package, 1280x800 viewport, service workers blocked), a semaphore on concurrent pages, optional media blocking and a built-in ad/analytics domain block list.
how: api.ts launches one chromium with --no-sandbox style flags, then createContext builds a new context per /scrape call with userAgent, viewport, ignoreHTTPSErrors and serviceWorkers 'block', routes '**/*' to drop 13 ad domains and (BLOCK_MEDIA) png/jpg/gif/svg/mp3/mp4/webm patterns, and closes page and context in finally. Semaphore of MAX_CONCURRENT_PAGES (default 10) guards acquire/release. /health creates and closes a real context and page. JSON/text responses are returned from the network body, other pages from page.content(). Supports wait_after_load, check_selector, headers and skip_tls_verification, but no actions, screenshots or PDF.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's local chromiumoxide path has per-session contexts already; the cheap wins are the health probe that really opens a page and the explicit page semaphore (Quarry's lease pool is size 2 and has no idle reaper).
notes: Quality 3: simple and safe but minimal. Chromium runs with --no-sandbox in a container with cap_drop ALL.

name: Playwright SSRF containment: loopback filtering proxy plus per-request route check
what: Every request the browser makes is forced through a loopback proxy that refuses private/internal destinations, and each request is also checked again in Playwright's route handler; a blocked navigation is reported as a 403 result instead of an error.
how: startSSRFProxy runs a proxy-chain Server on 127.0.0.1 whose prepareRequestFunction calls isInternalHost (DNS lookup of all addresses, reject any non-unicast range via ipaddr.js, fail closed when lookup fails) and chains to the optional upstream PROXY_SERVER. createContext sets context proxy to this loopback port; the route handler calls assertSafeTargetUrl for http/https and internal-host checks and aborts with blockedbyclient while remembering a blocked navigation URL. Top-level /scrape pre-checks the URL too and returns pageStatusCode 403.
verevonRelevance: Closest to Quarry's pinned loopback egress proxy; the difference is that Firecrawl resolves twice (check, then proxy-chain connects), leaving a DNS-rebinding window that Quarry's resolve-once-and-pin design closes.
notes: Quality 3: strong layering, but lookup-then-connect is a TOCTOU gap. Earlier Verevon docs say results are cached for 30 s; the code does a plain lookup per request with no cache.

name: Cookie header seeded into the browser cookie jar at domain scope
what: A Cookie header sent with a scrape is converted into real browser cookies so they survive redirects (a raw header is dropped on redirect hops), scoped to the registrable-looking domain so sibling-subdomain redirects stay authenticated.
how: In /scrape the Cookie header is split into name/value pairs and added with context.addCookies using domain '.'+last two host labels and path '/'; user-agent is applied at context level; remaining headers go to setExtraHTTPHeaders. The two-label domain rule is a heuristic that breaks for multi-part public suffixes such as co.uk.
verevonRelevance: If Quarry accepts caller cookies for scrape, seed them into the context jar (not a header) and use the public-suffix list rather than the last-two-labels shortcut.
notes: The code comment explains the redirect-drop bug it fixes; the suffix heuristic is a latent bug.

name: Fire-engine job protocol: submit, poll, delete, typed result parsing
what: Browser scrapes go to the closed fire-engine as asynchronous jobs: POST a typed request, receive either a finished result or a jobId, poll every 500 ms with a small error budget, then delete the job. Large results are offloaded to GCS and rehydrated.
how: fireEngineScrape POSTs {base}/scrape through robustFetch (tryCount 3, status errors ignored) and validates the response against three zod schemas (success, processing, failed). performFireEngineScrape polls fireEngineCheckStatus every 500 ms, tolerates 3 unexpected errors, deletes the remote job after success, error or abort, optionally A/B-routes to a staging host, gunzips inline files with a 50 MB cap and unwraps JSON bodies. Failure strings are mapped to typed errors by substring matching ('Chrome error: ' to SSL or Site errors, 'Dns resolution error', 'proxies available for', 'failed to finish without timing out', 'Element').
verevonRelevance: This is the contract Verevon's own browser fleet would implement for scrape-class jobs (submit/poll/delete, instantReturn, priority, saveResultToStore, zeroDataRetention flag); the string-matched error mapping is the part to avoid.
notes: Quality 3: robust plumbing, fragile error typing. Request fields visible: format, headers, blockMedia, priority, instantReturn, geolocation, mobileProxy, autoProxy, timeout, maxAge, saveScrapeResultToGCS, zeroDataRetention, behaviorOverrides, profile.

name: Page actions lowered into one ordered action list with hard limits
what: waitFor, screenshots, branding scripts and cookie capture are compiled into the same ordered action list as user actions and executed as one atomic browser job. Requests are limited to 50 actions and 60 s of total waiting; nine action types exist.
how: scrapeURLWithFireEngineChromeCDP prepends a wait action for waitFor (capped at 30 s), appends user actions (metadata stripped), appends a screenshot action (fullPage, viewport up to 7680x4320, quality 1-100) for the screenshot format, an internal executeJavascript for branding and a getCookies action for audio/video/youtube. Schema: wait(ms|selector, exclusive), click(selector, all), write, press, scroll(direction, selector), scrape, screenshot, executeJavascript, pdf(landscape, scale, format). Results are split into screenshots, scrapes, javascriptReturns and pdfs. waitFor must be at most half the timeout.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has a public action schema gap (ActionRuntime exists but no route calls it); these limits and the 'everything is an action' lowering are a ready template for wiring it.
notes: Quality 3: standard capability behind a closed engine. The pdf action is not in openapi.json's action list (spec drift).

name: Fire-engine behaviour overrides expose hidden stealth heuristics
what: The request contract to fire-engine carries six behaviour toggles that reveal what the hosted browser normally does behind the scenes: per-site special handling, hiding the webdriver flag, a non-headless user agent, OS/platform selection, geo/country selection and automatic referrer. Safe Mode switches them all to the honest setting.
how: FireEngineScrapeRequestCommon.behaviorOverrides {disableSiteHandling, exposeWebdriver, useHeadlessUserAgent, disablePlatformSelection, disableCountrySelection, disableAutomaticReferrer}; safeModeParams maps ResolvedSafeMode booleans to them for both chrome-cdp and tlsclient requests. A SiteRestrictionError is raised when fire-engine reports failureReason 'site_protection' under disableSiteHandling.
verevonRelevance: Useful checklist for Quarry's dormant stealth.rs: automatic referrer, OS/platform consistency, country-matched locale and webdriver exposure are the knobs to model, each with an 'honest mode' switch for compliance profiles.
notes: Only the contract is visible; the behaviours themselves are closed (INF from field names).

name: Geolocation, locale, mobile and viewport as first-class scrape options
what: Scrapes can request a country (ISO code plus two special pools) and language list, mobile emulation, ad blocking and a screenshot viewport; these options also partition the cache and select geo proxies.
how: locationSchema validates ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 plus 'us-generic' and 'us-whitelist', defaulting to us-generic; options travel to fire-engine as geolocation and to browser sessions as lowercase country (BrowserOptions.location.country). The index variant key and index columns include mobile, blockAds, stealth, country and languages. blockAds defaults true; mobile defaults false.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has mobile viewport only (no geo, locale or timezone emulation); partitioning cache and proxy choice by country+language is the part to copy with it.

name: Iframe flattening via selector rewrite
what: includeTags and excludeTags selectors that mention iframe are rewritten to target a div marked as the original iframe, because the hosted browser inlines iframe content into the DOM.
how: transformIframeSelector replaces bare 'iframe' tokens with div[data-original-tag="iframe"] in includeTags and excludeTags during request parsing.
verevonRelevance: If Quarry's AX/DOM projection flattens frames, it should expose a stable marker attribute so selector filters keep working across frame boundaries.
notes: The inlining itself is done by closed fire-engine (INF from the marker name).

name: Rendered branding extraction by injected script, with non-render fast path
what: The branding format runs a bundled script inside the page after a default 2 s settle wait and returns design tokens; when only DOM data is needed, the request is steered away from the heavy render engine, and non-HTML pages drop branding with a warning instead of failing the scrape.
how: getBrandingScript builds an esbuild IIFE (extractBrandDesign) and injects it as an internal executeJavascript action; BRANDING_DEFAULT_WAIT_MS is 2000; shouldForceNonRender returns true for branding unless screenshots, non-DOM actions, audio/video or youtube need visual output; branding-not-supported errors on PDFs/documents/images remove the format and add a warning when other formats were requested; LLM and a TypeSafe-backed fast path interpret the extracted data.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's branding is static-HTML only; the injected-script approach (not WASM as older Verevon notes claim) is a bounded way to add rendered branding once screenshot/evaluate exist on the scrape path.
notes: GAP.md section 11.2 says the branding script is a WASM module; the code shows an esbuild-bundled IIFE.

name: Content-type and magic-byte routing of files found by the browser
what: When a browser or fetch engine lands on a PDF, Office file or image, the file is handed to the right parser even if the server mislabels it: the Content-Type header decides first, then magic bytes, and the browser-downloaded file is passed along so parsers never re-download it.
how: specialtyScrapeCheck throws AddFeatureError(['pdf'|'document'|'image']) with a prefetch descriptor. It checks GCS references (large PDF handoff), document and PDF content types, image types confirmed by byte sniffing and an OCR gate, then sniffs %PDF-, PK\x03\x04 (OOXML/ODF) and the OLE2 header for headerless or mislabeled bodies, excluding genuine ZIP media types, before rejecting archives, audio, video and executables as UnsupportedFileError. With fire-engine present, buildFallbackList routes file URLs straight to the browser engines and the file engines act as pure parsers; proxy tunnel failures in direct downloads convert to PDF/DocumentFetchProxyError which re-route through the browser.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's scrape runs readability over any body including PDFs and uses PDF/DOCX parsers only on the answer path; a content-type plus magic-byte router in the pipeline would fix both without new engines.
notes: Quality 5: handles real-world mislabeling (octet-stream, image/jp2 PDFs) and keeps antibot-aware retry budgets.

name: Profile requests never fall back to anonymous engines and never touch the shared cache
what: A scrape that names a persistent browser profile can run only on chrome-cdp engines (or on parsers fed by bytes the authenticated browser downloaded), and requests with custom headers, actions or a profile bypass the shared URL cache entirely, so personalised content cannot leak to or poison other callers.
how: buildFallbackList skips every non-chrome-cdp engine when meta.options.profile is set, except pdf/document/image parsers with a prefetch; hasCustomRequestContext (headers, actions, profile) disables both index reads (shouldUseIndex) and index writes (sendDocumentToIndex); profile is passed to fire-engine as {owner: teamId, name} and stripped under Safe Mode; a profile cannot be combined with lockdown (schema refinement), and browser sessions reject profiles under ZDR.
verevonRelevance: Directly relevant to Quarry profiles: an authenticated profile must pin the browser driver and bypass content-keyed caches; Quarry's cache is fingerprint-keyed and opt-in, but its profile snapshots are unencrypted, which this design does not address either.
notes: Quality 5: simple rule with strong isolation value.

name: Hangar hosted browser sessions: lifecycle, idempotent create, live view and recording
what: Hosted browser sessions (via the closed Hangar service) have a state machine (starting, running, suspending, suspended, resuming, stopping, stopped, failed), absolute and inactivity TTLs, a CDP URL, a read-only and an interactive live-view URL, optional HLS recording, ad blocking, country selection and named persistent profiles.
how: createHangarBrowser POSTs /v1/browsers?wait=30 with an Idempotency-Key, retries up to 3 times on 5xx, long-polls state until running (5 min deadline) and stops the browser if readiness fails; body fields max_lifetime_seconds, idle_timeout_seconds, live_view {enabled, interactive}, recording {enabled}, execution {enabled}. browserCreateRequestSchema: ttl 30-3600 (600), activityTtl 10-3600 (300), streamWebView (true), recordSession (false), blockAds (true), profile {name, saveChanges}, location.country, zeroDataRetention. browserSessionLinks returns cdpUrl, liveViewUrl, interactiveLiveViewUrl.
verevonRelevance: Mirrors what Verevon's browser grant plus Quarry session leases need: idle vs absolute TTL, suspend/resume, idempotent create and a separate profile resource; Quarry's run map has no idle reaper, so adopt both TTLs.
notes: Quality 4 as a contract; the service itself is closed. Interactive control URL equals the human-takeover primitive. Browser and interact APIs migrated to Hangar 2026-09-25 (git e26b2d80c, #4757).

name: Code execution inside the hosted browser sandbox
what: A session accepts code in node, python or bash that runs next to the browser with direct access to its page and context objects, returning stdout, a result, stderr, exit code and a truncation flag. This is how scripted interaction and the interact agent work.
how: executeHangarBrowser POSTs /execute with {code, language, timeout}; schema limits code to 100,000 bytes and timeout to 1-300 s (default 30), language default node. The interact agent runs bash commands for the agent-browser CLI; selectBrowserAgentTab runs node snippets that use page, context.pages() and a CDP session to align the CLI with the visible tab.
verevonRelevance: A bounded in-sandbox execution endpoint (size, time, language allowlist, truncation flag) is a safer alternative to Quarry's unrestricted evaluate action; it must sit behind approval and the broker grant.
notes: Safe Mode orgs are refused interactive browser sessions outright.

name: Scrape-to-interact session reconstitution by replaying the scrape
what: A finished scrape can be promoted to an interactive session: a new browser is created and the original URL, wait and actions are replayed to land on the same page state, then a prompt or code runs on top. An existing pre-created session can be adopted instead.
how: scrapeInteractInternal validates ownership (queue job or stored access row), derives replay context (state.replay or buildReplayContextFromScrape from the stored options), creates or adopts a session, and buildReplayScript generates the Playwright script with sanitised, clamped actions and an estimated timeout. Retention policy is inherited from the scrape so a ZDR scrape stays ZDR.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a clean bridge from a Quarry scrape job to a live agent/browser run (the omnibox and chat live-run panel could open 'continue interactively' from a result) without storing the session.
notes: Replay depends on stored scrape options; keyless or DB-less deployments return 501.

name: Site-specific official-API engines inside the scrape waterfall
what: For hostile or terms-sensitive sites the waterfall uses an official data source instead of rendering: Wikipedia through the Wikimedia Enterprise API and X/Twitter posts and profiles through xAI's X search, both returned as normal scrape results.
how: wikipedia engine (quality 500, half of Wikimedia URLs only) authenticates to Wikimedia Enterprise with a Redis-cached token behind a redlock so only one instance logs in; x-twitter engine (quality 1500, exclusive when no profile is requested) parses post/profile URLs, calls grok-4-1-fast through the AI SDK with a structured schema and records both token and per-post X Search cost. A non-200 x-twitter failure is fatal rather than waterfalling.
verevonRelevance: Overlaps integration-corev2: a URL-to-provider resolver in the Quarry waterfall (github.com, notion.so, google docs) that prefers a connected-account action over scraping would unify browsing and connectors, which today never meet.
notes: Wikipedia engine is randomly applied to about half of Wikimedia URLs (Math.random gate).

name: Convenience URL rewrites and operator-forced engines per domain
what: Non-scrapable Google Docs/Slides/Sheets/Drive URLs are rewritten to export URLs before fetching, and operators can force specific engines for domain patterns through configuration.
how: rewriteUrl maps docs.google.com document, presentation and spreadsheet ids and drive file ids to /export?format=html, /gviz/tq?tqx=out:html (preserving gid) and uc?export=download, skipping published /d/e/ pages; the original URL is kept in metadata.sourceURL. FORCED_ENGINE_DOMAINS is a JSON map of domain or wildcard pattern to one engine or an engine list, consulted when the request has no forceEngine.
verevonRelevance: Cheap, high-yield: add a rewrite table in Quarry's URL normalisation, and a per-domain driver override config next to PRESETS.md so ops can pin a driver without code changes.
notes: Google Docs rewrites only work for link-shared documents; for private docs the integration-corev2 connector is the right path.

name: Proxy tiers basic, enhanced, stealth and auto with automatic escalation
what: Requests choose a proxy tier. 'auto' (the code default) starts on the basic proxy and escalates to the stealth (mobile) proxy when the target returns 401/403/429 or fire-engine signals retryWithStealth; 'enhanced' and 'stealth' go straight to stealth engines; no credit surcharge applies.
how: scrapeOptionFields.proxy enum with prefault 'auto'; buildFeatureFlags maps stealth and enhanced to the stealthProxy flag; stealth engine variants carry negative quality; fire-engine requests set mobileProxy for stealthProxy and autoProxy for 'auto'; AddFeatureError(['stealthProxy']) is thrown on bot statuses or retryWithStealth and capped by the retry budget; Safe Mode downgrades any escalated tier to basic.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's proxy pool has sticky (org, host) hashing and EgressBroker health ordering but no residential or geo tier and no automatic tier escalation; a 'basic then mobile/residential on bot signals' ladder is the missing policy.
notes: Docs mismatch: openapi.json says the default is basic and lists no 'stealth'; code defaults to auto. The pool behind stealth is closed.

name: Self-host proxy plumbing for fetch and Playwright paths
what: Self-hosters point one upstream proxy at both the HTTP engine and the browser engine with a single set of variables.
how: PROXY_SERVER, PROXY_USERNAME and PROXY_PASSWORD feed undici ProxyAgent (Basic token) for fetch and downloads, and are chained behind the loopback filtering proxy in the Playwright service; the service logs a warning when no proxy is set. When a proxy is configured the socket-level private-IP check only sees the proxy, so a literal-IP/localhost pre-check is the only local guard.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's QUARRY_PROXY_POOL is richer (sticky hash, privacy approval); the lesson is the documented SSRF gap behind a proxy and the need for proxy-side destination filtering.
notes: safeFetch.ts itself says hostnames behind a proxy are resolved proxy-side and must be filtered by the proxy.

name: Per-domain engine calibration (engpicker): cheapest engine that matches Chrome
what: A background job samples a domain, scrapes ten indexed pages with Chrome and with the TLS client (each with and without stealth), has an LLM judge which scrapes were real, compares TLS output to Chrome output by edit distance, and stores a per-domain verdict (TlsClientOk, ChromeCdpRequired, Uncertain) that later promotes the cheaper engine.
how: engpicker_queue rows pick up a domain split level; processEngpickerJob samples URLs from the index, runs four forced-engine scrapes per URL, judges success with gpt-4o-mini, and calls the Rust computeEngpickerVerdict (strsim Levenshtein similarity, thresholds for similarity, success rate and CDP failure rate) to produce engpicker_verdicts. At scrape time __experimental_engpicker queries the verdict with a 250 ms cap and boosts tlsclient quality by 50 when TlsClientOk.
verevonRelevance: A cost-saving loop Verevon lacks: learn per host whether static/TLS suffices and record it in the EgressBroker/domain intelligence registry already proposed in SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md.
notes: Quality 4: sound idea, opt-in and experimental in the API. Depends on the URL index to sample real pages. Engpicker proof of concept 2025-12-05 (git 085aab713, #2501).

name: Connect-time SSRF guard on the HTTP path
what: Outbound fetches reject private and loopback destinations on the initial request and every redirect hop, and drop any socket whose connected remote address is private; webhooks use the same dispatcher.
how: getSecureDispatcher composes rejectPrivateIPLiteralTargets (IP literal and localhost check before each dispatch) and an agent 'connect' listener that destroys sockets whose remoteAddress range is not unicast (ipaddr.js), unless ALLOW_LOCAL_WEBHOOKS. Checking the connected socket address avoids a separate resolve-then-connect race. Request URL validation itself only requires http(s) and a TLD-shaped or IP host, so IP literals such as 169.254.169.254 pass schema validation and rely on the connect-time guard.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's resolve-once-and-pin plus redirect re-validation is stronger; the useful addition is the post-connect remote-address check as a second layer for drivers that resolve internally.
notes: With a proxy configured only literal targets are filtered locally; redirect limit is 5000. Pre-dispatch private-target rejection behind a proxy added 2026-09-30 (git #4864).

name: robots.txt: fetched through the waterfall, cached in the URL index, opt-in on scrape, enforced on crawl, Crawl-delay ignored
what: Crawls respect robots.txt by default (with ignoreRobotsTxt and a custom robots user agent); single scrapes check it only when a team flag or Safe Mode asks; robots.txt itself is fetched through the same engine waterfall so bot-protected hosts still work, and cached for a day. Crawl-delay is parsed but intentionally not applied.
how: fetchRobotsTxt calls scrapeURL on /robots.txt with forceEngine [index, fetch/tlsclient/CDP...], timeout 8 s, maxAge 1 day, team 'robots-txt'. shouldCheckRobots is true only for Safe Mode enforceRobots or team flag checkRobotsOnScrape and never under lockdown (it would be an outbound request). Crawl workers check the start URL and redirect targets with isRobotsAllowed and filterLinks records robotsBlocked URLs per crawl. A fetch failure fails open. The robotsCrawlDelay assignment in crawl controllers is commented out.
verevonRelevance: Quarry enforces robots only in /v1/map; adopting 'enforce on crawl, opt-in on scrape, fetch via the driver waterfall, fail open on fetch error, record blocked URLs' closes its largest compliance gap, and honouring Crawl-delay through the AIMD host scheduler would beat Firecrawl.
notes: Quality 3: good placement, but Crawl-delay is deliberately off and the fail-open default is a policy choice.

name: Domain blocklists, global and per organisation, with buffered hit logging
what: Sites can be blocked for everyone or for one organisation, with keyword exceptions (including regex) that re-allow specific URLs; every block is recorded asynchronously for review.
how: initializeBlocklist loads a global blob and org blobs from Postgres into memory; isUrlBlocked uses tldts domain parsing plus allowedKeywords (plain, regex: or /re/flags); hits are buffered (200 entries or 5 s) and batch-inserted into blocklist_hits; blocked URLs are re-checked after redirects and may be admitted only for the Exchange provider path. Rows are written by ops directly.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has control /v1/blocklists plus an edge snapshot file; the org-scoped keyword exceptions and hit logging with post-redirect re-check are small additions.
notes: No public blocklist API exists in Firecrawl either.

name: Threat protection: URL risk verdicts with a no-persistence ZDR boundary
what: Enterprise orgs can block scrapes and crawl discoveries by URL risk. The target URL is checked before any engine runs, redirect destinations are re-checked, discovered crawl links are filtered, and verdicts are never stored across requests.
how: checkUrl evaluates local rules (whitelist, blacklist, blocked TLD), optionally Zscaler synced custom-list rules, then a provider (Google Web Risk hash-prefix database or batched Zscaler lookup) with a 5 s timeout and one retry; failurePolicy decides fail-open or fail-closed; a request-scoped dedup map avoids double scans; map results in zscaler mode use localRulesOnly to avoid burning lookup quota. Billing: +2 credits per unique scanned URL. scrapeURL re-checks the final URL when canonical URLs differ.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's security preflight is heuristics plus a blocklist; a hash-prefix reputation feed with an explicit failure policy and no persisted verdicts fits Verevon's ZDR-must-propagate rule.
notes: Quality 4. Web Risk uses a local hash-prefix database, so full URLs are not sent to Google for most checks (INF from module names). Introduced 2026-07-07 (git 6db599637, #3949).

name: Safe Mode: an organisation-enforced compliance profile that requests cannot widen
what: A single org flag switches a bundle of safer behaviours on: robots enforced, no stealth proxy, no credential headers, cookies or login actions, URL userinfo stripped, domain controls, honest browser behaviour toggles, optional lockdown, and no interactive browser sessions. Per-request opt-out exists only if the org allows it.
how: resolveSafeMode returns ResolvedSafeMode (defaults all on except lockdown) or an error; applySafeMode downgrades proxy to basic and forces lockdown; scrapeURL re-resolves per URL as a backstop for crawl children and strips Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization headers, write/press/executeJavascript actions, profile and URL userinfo; browser and interact endpoints and v0 endpoints return 403 for Safe Mode orgs; allowlisted domains bypass.
verevonRelevance: Maps cleanly onto Quarry's RunPolicy presets and the 'space access never widens owner ACL' rule: an org-pinned policy tier enforced at the worker backstop, not only at the HTTP edge.
notes: Quality 5: enforced at both request time and worker time so inherited options in crawl children cannot bypass it. Introduced 2026-09-15 (git f62a24c5d, #4612).

name: Lockdown: cache-only scraping with zero outbound traffic
what: Lockdown serves only from the stored URL index (default max age two years), never fetches the target, robots, sitemaps or redirects, implies zero data retention and costs 4 extra credits; a miss returns a typed 'lockdown cache miss' error.
how: scrapeOptions.lockdown with LOCKDOWN_DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MS; buildFlags returns no features; buildFallbackList pins forceEngine to index and index;documents; shouldCheckRobots returns false; getMapResults and crawler sitemap discovery return index-only results; LockdownMissError is thrown when no engine is left.
verevonRelevance: A natural 'no-egress' mode for Verevon workspaces: answer from Data Plane/Quarry artifacts only and guarantee no outbound requests, aligned with ZDR and sovereign-data positioning.
notes: Naming collision with 'lockdown' used elsewhere; here it only concerns scraping egress.

name: Tiered URL content cache (Redis hot path, Postgres metadata, GCS bodies)
what: Scraped pages are cached as raw HTML in object storage with URL and domain-split hashes in a separate Postgres index, fronted by an LRU Redis (Dragonfly) cache that fails fast; formats are re-derived from the cached HTML on every hit, so one entry serves many format requests.
how: sendDocumentToIndex writes <indexId>.json to GCS and queues an index insert job (url_split_0..9 and domain_splits_0..4 hash columns, mobile, blockAds, stealth, country, languages, screenshot and wait metadata, invalidated_at). scrapeURLWithIndex looks up Redis entries (cap 32 per variant key, 7 day TTL, 150 ms read timeout, offline queue disabled) then falls back to index_get_recent_5 in Postgres, loads the body from GCS (self-healing if the object is gone) and returns an EngineScrapeResult with cacheInfo. The engine has 1.5 s max reasonable time.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's cache is fingerprint-keyed and only hits when the caller supplies prev_fingerprint; a URL-keyed maxAge cache of raw bodies (artifact store plus metadata index) is the biggest missing latency and cost lever, and must carry ZDR and org scoping.
notes: Quality 5: tiered, fail-fast and self-healing. Index DB, cache and GCS are closed infrastructure; Firecrawl caches public pages across tenants. URL index introduced 2025-06-03 (git 95f204aab, #1605).

name: Cache write policy: what must never be cached
what: Only rendered or API-quality results are cached: results from the TLS client or plain fetch are not written (except sitemaps), nor are ZDR, parse uploads, requests with headers, actions or profiles, custom screenshot sizes, truncated PDFs, page-aware PDF variants or Exchange results.
how: sendDocumentToIndex computes shouldCache from storeInCache, isParse, zeroDataRetention, winnerEngine (not index, exchange, fetch or tlsclient unless team 'sitemap'), unparsed-PDF, page markdown/blocks/markers parsers, isTruncatedPdf, actions, custom screenshot settings and hasCustomRequestContext. shouldUseIndex applies the same gating on reads plus changeTracking and branding formats and maxAge 0. A cached unparsed PDF is reported as a miss when parsing is requested and vice versa.
verevonRelevance: A ready checklist for Quarry's cache admission policy; note redactPII is not part of the exclusion list (the raw HTML of a PII-redacted request is still stored in the shared index, INF from the conditions), which Verevon must decide explicitly.
notes: Quality 5: explicit and test-covered (index-cache and scrape-cache snips).

name: Freshness controls: maxAge, minAge, dynamic domain max age and store opt-out
what: Callers choose cache freshness with maxAge (ms), can demand data at least minAge old (no live fetch, a 404-style error on miss), and opt out of storing; without maxAge the default is two days or a per-domain dynamic value looked up with a 200 ms cap.
how: scrapeURLWithIndex resolves maxAge as explicit, dynamic_cached (Redis, 15 min TTL), dynamic_db (query_max_age) or default 2 days, racing a 200 ms timer; filterIndexEntries and index_get_recent_5 apply maxAge, minAge, screenshot capability and waitFor >= requested; selection prefers the newest 2xx unless it is more than 3 entries back; NoCachedDataError when minAge and no entry; storeInCache defaults true.
verevonRelevance: Gives Quarry the missing maxAge/minAge vocabulary (and the 'serve error entry only if 2xx is older than 3 tries' rule) for its PRESETS.md stale-while-revalidate intent that is not implemented.
notes: The default is 2 days, not 'no cache'; docs should be read with this in mind.

name: Negative caching and cache poison self-healing
what: Confirmed misses are remembered so repeat lookups skip Postgres, and a cache entry pointing at a missing GCS body is deleted automatically.
how: setCachedNegative records the left edge of the empty window under idxcneg:<variant>; getCachedNegative plus isNegativeStillValid skips the DB when still valid (not used for filtered or error reads or minAge); INDEX_CACHE_NEGATIVE_TTL_MS defaults to 0 (opt-in); a missing GCS document deletes the Redis entry and logs a warning with canonical outcome labels counted in indexLookupCounter.
verevonRelevance: Small pattern worth copying for Quarry's search-router cache and any future URL cache: negative entries with window semantics and self-heal on dangling artifact refs.

name: Demand-driven precrawl to keep hot domains warm
what: A scheduled admin-triggered job selects domains with enough recent demand, allocates a page budget in proportion to the square root of their priority, and crawls their most-requested URLs to refresh the cache before users ask.
how: processPrecrawlJob queries domains with at least 1000 events and priority >= 4 (up to 500 domains, 25,000-page budget, 10-50 URLs per domain), sorts by sqrt priority, queries top URLs from the last 8 days in batches of 25 with backoff, and submits crawl jobs flagged isPreCrawl under PRECRAWL_TEAM_ID. The admin route triggers it.
verevonRelevance: Quarry already tracks sources ('tracked websites') and schedules change monitors; a demand-weighted refresh budget for hot sources would make its fingerprint cache effective.
notes: Needs usage events in the index DB; closed infra.

name: API rate limiting per endpoint class scaled by plan multiplier
what: Per-minute limits are defined per endpoint class (scrape, crawl, search, map, extract, browser, browser execute, status polling and more) as base values times the team's plan multiplier, with per-org overrides and a hobby floor for trusted agent traffic.
how: rate-limiter-flexible with Redis; BASE_RATE_LIMITS (scrape 10, crawl 2, extract 2, browser 2, browserExecute 10, status 500) multiplied by Autumn's rate_limits feature; getRateLimitOverride lets org flags replace the whole computation; fallback table with browser 2, crawlStatus 25000; agent-interop trusted requests are floored at the hobby multiplier.
verevonRelevance: Verevon enforces limits in Control Plane quotas; the endpoint-class split (cheap polling vs expensive browser) and the fail-open behaviour on entitlement outage are the design points to copy.
notes: The auth chunk (ACUC) is cached for 10 minutes and fails open for 60 s when the entitlement service is unavailable.

name: Crawl politeness is coarse: a crawl delay serialises the crawl and sleeps in the promotion loop
what: The only politeness control is a crawl-level 'delay' option; when set, the crawl is limited to one concurrent job and each promotion waits that many seconds. There is no per-host adaptive throttle and robots Crawl-delay is not applied.
how: getNextConcurrentJob sets max crawl concurrency to 1 when crawlerOptions.delay > 0; concurrentJobDone sleeps delay seconds inside the team's promotion loop; the FDB backend stores per-group delaySeconds and maxConcurrency; controllers pass maxConcurrency capped by the team limit.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's AIMD per-host scheduler plus global autoscaled pool are clearly ahead here; do not copy this, but do copy the per-crawl maxConcurrency cap.
notes: Quality 2: the sleep blocks promotion for every job of the team.

name: Three-tier abort model and timeout budgeting
what: Each scrape carries external, scrape and engine abort tiers; a scrape timeout cancels everything, an engine timeout only cancels that engine, and sync requests spend two thirds of their timeout budget waiting for a concurrency slot at most.
how: AbortManager composes AbortInstances tagged external, scrape or engine with throwable factories, exposes asSignal, scrapeTimeout and engineNearestTimeout, and wraps thrown reasons in AbortManagerThrownError so loops can tell tiers apart; sync scrape aborts the semaphore wait at 0.667 x timeout and on client disconnect; waitFor must be at most half the timeout.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's tokio CancellationToken is flat; layering client-gone, request-deadline and per-driver tokens (with typed reasons) would make hedging and escalation safe.
notes: Earlier Verevon notes describe an 'abort(jobId)' singleton; the code is per-scrape and tiered.

name: Typed error-code vocabulary that survives queues and carries retry hints
what: Scrape failures are typed with about 55 stable error codes (all engines failed, SSL, DNS, PDF antibot, lockdown miss, prompt injection detected, retry limit...) that cross the queue and webhook boundary; timeouts of long PDF jobs return a 'processing continues' block with estimated remaining time and a Retry-After.
how: ErrorCodes union and TransportableError with serialize/deserialize; scrapeURL error classes extend it; composeTimeoutProcessing builds details {state: processing_continues, jobStatus, estimatedRemainingSeconds, retryAfterSeconds, mayExceedProcessingWindow} from live FirePDF job state; DNS errors return HTTP 200 success:false; other codes map to 4xx/5xx.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has typed failure codes on its improvement list; this vocabulary (plus the retry-after contract for work that outlives the request) is a ready list of codes for the scrape, crawl and agent surfaces.

name: Request idempotency is key-reuse rejection only
what: An x-idempotency-key (UUID) header makes a second request with the same key fail with 409 instead of replaying the first response.
how: validateIdempotencyKey checks the key against the idempotency_keys table; idempotencyMiddleware returns 409 'Idempotency key already used' and otherwise records the key; the paid provider path has a richer replaying design (see Alexandria).
verevonRelevance: For Quarry's mutating endpoints use the Alexandria-style store (completed replays response, mismatched payload 409, in-flight 409, uncertain 503) rather than this key-only check.

name: Option-dependent defaults: TLS verification relaxed unless credentials are sent, timeouts widened by feature
what: Scrapes skip TLS certificate verification by default so sites with bad certificates still work, but verification is switched back on whenever custom headers or actions (possible credentials) are present; default timeouts are automatically raised for JSON extraction, change tracking and stealth/auto proxy requests.
how: applyScrapeOptionsDefaults sets skipTlsVerification to false when headers or actions are present and true otherwise; extractTransformImpl raises a default 30 s timeout to 60 s for json and changeTracking formats (also forcing waitFor >= 5 s for change tracking) and to 120 s when proxy is stealth, enhanced or auto; lockdown fills maxAge with two years; fire-engine and parsers receive the resolved flag.
verevonRelevance: A sound default pair for Quarry: relax certificate errors only for anonymous reads, and make time budgets a function of the requested features instead of one global timeout.
notes: Relaxed TLS on anonymous reads trades integrity for coverage; Verevon should expose it as an explicit policy field recorded in the receipt.

name: NuQ: a Postgres job queue built on SKIP LOCKED, partial indexes and pg_cron
what: Durable scrape and crawl-finish queues live in Postgres. Workers claim the lowest priority-number, oldest job with row locking, renew a lock every 15 s, and a 15-second pg_cron reaper requeues stalled jobs up to nine times before failing them and notifying listeners.
how: nuq.queue_scrape(id, status queued/active/completed/failed, data jsonb, priority, lock, locked_at, stalls, group_id, owner_id, listen_channel_id) with partial indexes per status; getJobToProcess runs WITH next AS (... ORDER BY priority, created_at FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1) UPDATE ... SET status='active', lock=gen_random_uuid(); renewLock updates locked_at only if lock and status still match; the reaper cron requeues locked_at older than 1 minute with stalls < 9, else fails and pg_notify's 'id|failed'. Completed standalone rows are purged after 1 h, failed after 6 h; autovacuum is tuned aggressively per queue table. pgbouncer-style pool for queries, a direct connection for LISTEN.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has a Postgres SKIP LOCKED queue bridge for the durable frontier and Temporal for workflows; NuQ shows how far a single Postgres queue goes (lock renewal, stall counters, partial indexes) and what operational tuning it needs.
notes: Quality 4: deeply tuned, with comments recording production measurements (18M-row tables, 12 indexes). Complexity is real: reindex schedules and a watchdog are part of the design.

name: RabbitMQ prefetch layer and per-pod completion listeners in front of Postgres
what: A prefetch worker moves up to 500 queued jobs to the active state in one statement and publishes them to RabbitMQ so that workers pull from the broker instead of hammering Postgres; workers fall back to Postgres if the broker is unavailable. Job completion is delivered to the waiting API pod over a per-pod queue or LISTEN/NOTIFY.
how: prefetchJobs updates up to 500 rows (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 500) and sends each to '<queue>.prefetch'; getJobToProcess calls channel.get(noAck) on that queue and resets the sender on failure, falling back to the SQL claim; listenable jobs carry listen_channel_id (pod name + uuid) and sendJobEnd publishes to '<queue>.listen.<channel>'; without RabbitMQ a LISTEN client on a direct DB URL receives pg_notify. Idle workers back off 1.5 s doubling to 10 s only when RabbitMQ is not used.
verevonRelevance: Relevant if Quarry's Postgres request queue becomes a contention point: batch-claim plus broker fan-out with graceful fallback keeps the database off the hot path; NATS/JetStream (already in the Verevon stack) could play the broker role.
notes: Prefetched jobs are already 'active' with locks, so the reaper still protects against a lost broker message.

name: Crawl groups: completion by cron, backlog with expiry, TTL-based batch cleanup
what: A crawl is a group of jobs. A cron detects when a group has no queued, active or backlogged jobs, marks it completed and enqueues a single 'crawl finished' job that runs finalisation (billing summary, webhooks, notifications). Over-limit jobs wait in a backlog table with an expiry, and completed groups are deleted in small batches after their TTL.
how: nuq.group_crawl (status, owner_id, ttl default 24 h, expires_at); nuq_group_crawl_finished cron every 15 s inserts a queue_crawl_finished row when no queue_scrape or backlog rows remain; queue_scrape_backlog(times_out_at) is reaped every minute; nuq_group_crawl_clean deletes 500 expired groups per minute with SKIP LOCKED and a 90 s statement timeout, cascading to all three queue tables. finishCrawlSuper then logs the crawl, reads billed credits from Bigtable request-credit shards (ClickHouse fallback with retries) and sends webhooks and in-app notifications.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's crawl completion lives inside a Temporal workflow loop; the 'completion is derived from the queue being empty and emits one finalise job' pattern is useful if Verevon moves crawl fan-out into the durable frontier.
notes: Group completion is eventually consistent by up to 15 s.

name: FoundationDB queue backend with slot gating and a dual-backend router
what: An alternative queue backend on FoundationDB models team, crawl and API-key concurrency slots directly in the queue (pending, queued, active states), shards ready jobs, tracks group concurrency and start delays, and is adopted per team with each crawl pinned to one backend.
how: nuq-fdb keyspace under ('nuq', queue) with atomic ADD counters, ready shards, team-pending shards, time buckets, a delay index and a sweeper; job meta flags F_GATED, F_CRAWL_GATED, F_KEY_GATED, F_LISTENABLE, F_ZDR, F_COUNTABLE; GroupMeta {maxConcurrency, delaySeconds, ttl}; nuq-router exposes the same queue names, decides new work by team flag nuqFdb or NUQ_BACKEND=fdb, pins StoredCrawl.queueBackend, defaults unmarked reads to Postgres, and falls back to Postgres with throttled warnings when FDB health checks fail. Compose ships foundationdb 7.3.63 plus an init job.
verevonRelevance: Not something Verevon should adopt, but the idea that concurrency gates (team, crawl, key) belong inside the queue rather than in a side Redis structure is worth weighing against Quarry's current in-process lease pool and per-host scheduler.
notes: Marked experimental in Compose. The migration mechanism (flag per team, crawl pinned, default old backend) is a good template for any store swap. Queue rebuilt on FoundationDB 2026-06-12 (git b9eb2faec, #3758).

name: Sync scrapes run in-process behind a per-team lease semaphore; only async work is queued
what: A synchronous scrape does not touch the queue: the API process takes a per-team concurrency lease (waiting up to two thirds of the request timeout), runs the scrape pipeline directly and releases the lease; crawl, batch and monitor work goes through NuQ.
how: scrapeController wraps processJobInternal (job built with skipNuq: true) in teamConcurrencySemaphore.withSemaphore(team, jobId, concurrency, abort, timeout); a Redis Lua lease (zset with holder TTL 30 s, heartbeat) enforces the team limit; acquireBlocking retries with exponential backoff 1.5x and jitter until the deadline then throws ConcurrencyQueueTimeoutError; req.on('close') aborts; dynamic job priority is computed from the team's in-flight set.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's /v1/scrape already runs inline on the edge fast path; the distinguishing pieces to copy are lease heartbeats with TTL, backoff with jitter on admission and aborting on client disconnect.

name: Concurrency queue with promotion and per-crawl concurrency limits
what: When a team is at its concurrency limit, extra jobs wait in a Redis sorted-set queue and are promoted as running jobs finish, honouring a per-crawl concurrency cap; a reconciler repairs drift between the Postgres backlog and the Redis queue every minute.
how: pushConcurrencyLimitedJob stores job payloads under per-team keys; getNextConcurrentJob ZPOPMINs candidates, drops expired entries, holds back jobs whose crawl is at maxConcurrency (1 when a delay is set) and re-adds them in finally; concurrentJobDone promotes up to the team limit into scrapeQueue.promoteJobFromBacklogOrAdd and removes stale entries (max 100 per pass); the reconciler worker runs reconcileConcurrencyQueue and repairCrawlJobDoneMarkers each 60 s and exposes Prometheus counters.
verevonRelevance: Shows the failure mode of keeping the same truth in two stores (Postgres backlog and Redis queue need a reconciler); Quarry should keep concurrency state in one place.
notes: The FDB backend exists partly to remove this dual-store drift.

name: Fair-share dynamic job priority based on a team's in-flight jobs
what: A team's jobs get progressively lower priority as it keeps more jobs in flight within a 60-second window, with the threshold and slope depending on the plan tier, so a large crawl from one customer cannot starve the rest.
how: getJobPriority keeps a Redis set per team (expiring after 60 s), reads the plan tier inferred from the Autumn rate-limit multiplier (PLAN_PRIORITY_TIERS with bucketLimit and planModifier), returns the base priority up to bucketLimit and base + ceil((count - bucketLimit) * planModifier) beyond it; kickoff 15, sitemap/index 21 and sync 10 are base priorities; lower number runs first.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has no cross-org fairness on its request queue; a per-org in-flight-based priority penalty is a small change in the Postgres queue's priority column that protects multi-tenant latency.
notes: Inferring plan priority from the rate-limit multiplier is flagged in comments as safe because it only shifts ordering.

name: Worker admission control on CPU and memory with stall detection
what: A worker refuses to pull new jobs when host CPU or memory is above 80 percent (cgroup-aware under Kubernetes), reports itself stalled after 25 consecutive refusals, and also refuses while its liveness check fails.
how: SystemMonitor.acceptConnection compares CPU and RAM usage (systeminformation, or /sys/fs/cgroup memory.current and memory.max in Kubernetes) with MAX_CPU and MAX_RAM (default 0.8) using cached readings; queue-worker loops sleep when it returns false, log 'WORKER STALLED' with the readings after 25 refusals and gate on currentLiveness.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has a global AutoscaledPool on the fast path but none on browser leases; a memory-aware admission gate on the Chromium host would stop renderer OOMs when concurrent sessions pile up.

name: Worker runner: lock renewal, graceful drain, per-process health and metrics, one-container supervisor
what: Every worker process serves /health and /metrics on its own port, renews its job lock every 15 s, stops accepting work on SIGTERM while finishing active jobs, and a harness supervisor starts the API, queue workers, prefetch worker, reconciler, extract worker and index worker inside one container.
how: runNuqWorker builds an Express app with /metrics (local queue metrics plus prom-client registry) and /health (1 s timeout), loops getJobToProcess with backoff, sets setInterval renewLock(15 s), records jobDurationSeconds and calls jobFinish or jobFail with serialised errors; harness.ts spawns NUQ_WORKER_COUNT (default 5) workers on consecutive ports plus prefetch and reconciler workers and colour-prefixed log forwarding; API shutdown waits 60 s for the cloud load balancer to drain when IS_KUBERNETES.
verevonRelevance: A single-binary multi-process supervisor with per-process health and metrics ports is a convenient dev and self-host story for Quarry's edge, control and orchestrator trio.
notes: In production the processes are split across pods; the harness is for dev, CI and the Docker default.

name: Crawl state in Redis: visited sets, permutation-based URL dedupe and redirect reconciliation
what: Crawl progress is kept in Redis with a 24-hour TTL: URLs are locked in a visited set before queueing, www/http/https/trailing-slash/index.html variants can be treated as one URL, the crawl limit counts unique URLs, and a redirect target is re-locked and checked so the same page is not crawled twice.
how: lockURL SADDs the normalised URL (hash routes preserved, query stripped when ignoreQueryParameters, fragment dropped) to crawl:<id>:visited, optionally locking generateURLPermutations(...)[0] when deduplicateSimilarURLs is set, and counts crawl:<id>:visited_unique against the limit; keys jobs, jobs_done, jobs_donez_ordered, kickoff:finish, robots_blocked, threat_blocked, finish expire after 24 h and finishCrawl deletes the heavy sets; processJob locks the redirected URL's permutations and throws RacedRedirectError if another job already holds it; addCrawlJobDone has a repair queue for lost done markers.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's workflow dedupes by exact string; adopting a normalisation plus permutation set (the file documents the three algebraic properties permutations must satisfy) is a cheap crawl-quality win.
notes: State lives in Redis, which Verevon's GAP.md lists as a Firecrawl weakness (lost on restart); the 24 h TTL is an explicit trade-off.

name: Crawl scope and link filtering in Rust with typed denial reasons and a JS fallback
what: Link discovery filters candidates by depth, include/exclude regexes (path or full URL), path hierarchy (backward crawling off by default), domain, subdomain, social media, non-web protocols, file extensions, fragments and robots; each rejected URL gets a typed reason. The same logic exists natively and in TypeScript, with fallback on native failure.
how: filter_links in the napi crate returns allowed links and a denial map using constants DEPTH_LIMIT, EXCLUDE_PATTERN, INCLUDE_PATTERN, BACKWARD_CRAWLING, ROBOTS_TXT, FILE_TYPE, SOCIAL_MEDIA, EXTERNAL_LINK, SECTION_LINK, NON_WEB_PROTOCOL, URL_PARSE_ERROR; crawl scope = directory prefix (plus exact path when the last segment has no extension) shared with lib/crawl-scope.ts ('keep in sync'); validate_regexes and regex-count/length caps (1000 patterns, 2000 chars each, 100,000 total) guard ReDoS-style input; options: includePaths, excludePaths, maxDepth, maxDiscoveryDepth, allowBackwardLinks, crawlEntireDomain, allowSubdomains, allowExternalLinks, ignoreQueryParameters, regexOnFullURL, limit (default 10,000).
verevonRelevance: Quarry's Rust CrawlFrontier (scope, globs, CrawlDenialReason) is the same design but is not wired into the live Go crawl path; Firecrawl proves the value of making the filter the single enforcement point with typed reasons.
notes: Dual native+JS implementation doubles maintenance risk but gives a safe fallback.

name: Denial reasons written as remediation advice for LLM and human callers
what: Every URL a crawl refuses comes with a plain-language sentence naming the option that caused it and how to change it (for example which excludePaths pattern matched, or to set allowBackwardCrawling or crawlEntireDomain), and these are returned in the crawl errors endpoint.
how: DenialReason enum messages plus 'fancy' per-URL messages built in WebCrawler.filterLinks (the actual matched exclude pattern, URL depth versus maxDepth, the scope prefix); CrawlDenialError carries the reason; robots-blocked and threat-blocked URLs are recorded in separate Redis lists per crawl.
verevonRelevance: Because Verevon's callers are agents, refusal messages that tell the model how to fix the request (and map to Quarry's typed denial codes) improve agent recovery with no new infrastructure.

name: Crawl kickoff: start-page scrape, multi-source sitemap discovery and index-assisted seeding
what: A crawl begins with a kickoff job that scrapes the start page, then discovers URLs from robots.txt Sitemap lines, a sitemap in the scoped directory, /sitemap.xml and the registrable-domain sitemap, and also seeds from URLs the cache index already knows for that domain, so large sites start fast.
how: processKickoffJob locks and queues the source scrape (isCrawlSourceScrape, checked against robots), emits crawl.started, queues kickoff_sitemap jobs per candidate (nested sitemaps up to SITEMAP_LIMIT 25, 3 fetched concurrently, results streamed through a Redis set to dedupe, sitemaps fetched via scrapeURL with a 7-day maxAge), calls kickoffGetIndexLinks for already-indexed URLs, filters them through threat protection and enqueues with lock-then-add semantics at priority 21; native parse_sitemap_xml and process_sitemap handle index versus urlset and instruct fetches; gz sitemaps are decompressed.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's workflow does no sitemap seeding; copy the candidate list (robots Sitemap lines, scoped dir, root, registrable domain) and index-assisted seeding using Quarry's own source/snapshot store.
notes: Index-assisted seeding depends on a populated URL index.

name: Crawl budget capped by remaining credits and per-request credit shards
what: A crawl's page limit is silently reduced to the team's remaining credits, crawl results live for a configurable number of hours, and per-request credit accounting uses sharded counters so very large crawls do not contend on one row.
how: crawl controller sets finalCrawlerOptions.limit = min(remainingCredits, limit), calls initializeRequestCredits with requestCreditsShards(limit) (Bigtable), saves StoredCrawl with maxConcurrency capped to the team limit and crawlTtlHours from team flags (default 24); finishCrawlSuper reads the sharded sum at the end.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has no org cost budget on crawls; clamping the crawl limit to the Control Plane's remaining entitlement at submit time (and recording the clamped value) is the minimal budget guard.

name: Monitor scheduler: lease claim, overlap skipping, hash jitter, stale-run recovery and credit reservation
what: Recurring monitors (scrape, crawl or search targets) are claimed by schedulers with leases, deferred by a deterministic jitter so many monitors do not fire together, skipped with a recorded 'skipped_overlap' when the previous run is still going, healed when a run is stale, and reserve credits per run.
how: enqueueDueMonitorChecks claims due monitors (workerId, limit, leaseSeconds), deferForJitter uses sha256(monitorId) mod min(interval/2, 5 min), createMonitorCheck/dispatchScheduledMonitorCheck/advanceMonitorAfterSkippedCheck update state, isMonitorCheckStale uses 60 min (10 min for search-only monitors), cron.ts validates 5-field cron with a 5-minute minimum interval and also parses phrases like 'every 30 minutes' or 'daily at 9:00 am'; run statuses include queued, running, completed, failed, partial, skipped_overlap, skipped_no_credits with credit reservation states.
verevonRelevance: Quarry can only execute change_monitor schedules (trigger and backfill return 501); the lease-claim, skipped_overlap, jitter and stale-recovery set is the missing operational layer around its Temporal reconciler.
notes: Quality 4. Scheduling is a DB claim loop, not Temporal; both are valid. Monitor API orchestration added 2026-05-06 (git bc3c57adb, #3470).

name: Map: union of cache index, sitemaps and search discovery with relevance reranking
what: Whole-site URL discovery merges URLs from the URL index, sitemaps and (in the cloud) site-scoped search results, resolves redirects first, filters by path and robots, and ranks by cosine similarity to an optional query; under lockdown it uses the index only.
how: getMapResults resolves redirects (skipped under lockdown), builds a StoredCrawl for scope rules, fetches robots, runs tryGetSitemap or queryIndex (generateURLSplits, domain split levels) and fireEngineMap (up to 100 results), dedupes by URL preferring entries with titles, applies map-cosine reranking for search, and caps at MAX_MAP_LIMIT; sitemap-only mode lifts the limit.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's /v1/map reads one sitemap plus seed links; adding index-assisted discovery (its own tracked sources) and robots Sitemap lines is the upgrade path.
notes: Only the first 200 lines of map-utils were read; later ranking code is not verified.

name: Multi-step extract workflow with recorded steps in Redis
what: The legacy multi-page extract runs as a staged workflow (map, rerank, multi-entity detection, scrape, extract) and records each step with discovered links so callers can inspect progress; state expires after 6 hours.
how: ExtractStep enum INITIAL, MAP, MAP_RERANK, MULTI_ENTITY, MULTI_ENTITY_SCRAPE, MULTI_ENTITY_EXTRACT, SCRAPE, EXTRACT; saveExtract stores minimal state (status, steps with startedAt/finishedAt, sources, llmUsage, creditsBilled, costTracking) with a 6 h TTL and a cap of 100 discovered links per step; the pipeline lives in lib/extract/fire-0 (url-processor, reranker, document-scraper, extraction-service, source-tracker). The current agent-based extract is an external service.
verevonRelevance: If Quarry's /v1/extract grows beyond 25 sequential URLs, a recorded-step workflow (visible to the UI timeline) is the model; Temporal already gives the durability Firecrawl hand-rolls in Redis.
notes: Only headers and state types were read; step internals are not verified.

name: Zero-data-retention-aware tracing: unrecorded spans, late-discovery registry and export-time drop
what: Spans for requests under zero data retention are never recorded or exported, including spans created by third-party libraries such as the AI SDK, and traces that learn they are ZDR only after starting are dropped before export.
how: withZeroDataRetention sets an OpenTelemetry context key; ZeroDataRetentionSampler returns NOT_RECORD for ZDR context or attributes zero_data_retention=true, registers late-flagged trace ids in a bounded set (100,000) so descendants are unrecorded and in-flight spans dropped at end; isZeroDataRetentionActive lets code switch off AI SDK experimental_telemetry; tracing is off unless an OTLP endpoint is configured; withSpan takes a zeroDataRetention option; queue bookkeeping and job failure recording also run under the ZDR context.
verevonRelevance: Directly answers Verevon's 'ZDR must propagate through any content-persisting boundary' for observability: Quarry's OTLP tracing and ZDR events need a sampler-level guarantee rather than per-call checks.
notes: Quality 5: sampler plus export-time defence in depth, with comments explaining each layer. Tracing rebuilt 2025-09-27 (git 2bf969264, #2219); ZDR sampler layers added later.

name: ZDR across process boundaries: log filter, header propagation, monotonic retention and delayed cleanup
what: Zero data retention is carried everywhere content could stick: log lines tagged ZDR are dropped by the logger, downstream helper services receive an X-Zero-Data-Retention header and skip request-correlated logs, retention policy of a session can only get stricter, and results retained for async retrieval are deleted by a 24-hour delayed queue.
how: winston zeroDataRetentionFilter returns false for metadata.zeroDataRetention; Go html-to-md service checks X-Zero-Data-Retention and omits request ids from logs; browser sessions reject ZDR with recordings or profiles (400) and refuse to upgrade an existing non-ZDR session (409), inherit ZDR from the scrape when interacting and read stored policy under a ZDR context first so lookup telemetry cannot leak; zdr-queue is a RabbitMQ quorum delay queue (24 h TTL, dead-letter to a ready queue, DLQ); cleanZdrRequest finds blobs via a ClickHouse request_children index and deletes them from GCS; change tracking, async FirePDF jobs, caching and the A/B mirror are disabled for ZDR requests.
verevonRelevance: Provides a concrete checklist for Verevon's ZDR rule across Quarry, billing, notification and Model Plane calls; note Firecrawl's ZDR retains results for up to 24 h for async retrieval, whereas Quarry's ZDR scrape returns no page content at all, so the product trade-off should be made explicitly.
notes: Quality 5. Earlier Verevon notes say ZDR results are never written to Redis or Postgres; the code shows 24 h blob retention then deletion for async jobs. ZDR cleanup moved to RabbitMQ 2026-09-16 (git 90fd89cdc, #4650).

name: Prometheus metrics per process plus canonical log lines for hot paths
what: Every worker and the API expose Prometheus metrics (queue, semaphores, PDF extraction, FirePDF, index cache, webhooks, SIEM, keyless, event-loop lag, heap and GC), and hot paths emit one canonical log record per operation with a fixed outcome label.
how: prom-client registries exposed on each worker's /metrics and admin metrics endpoints; examples: pdf_extraction_semaphore_active/waiting/wait_seconds/hold_seconds, noq_semaphore_*, concurrency_queue_reconciler_*, firecrawl_nuq_fdb_pending_jobs, index lookup counter with outcomes cache_hit, cache_neg_hit, cache_miss_db_hit, db_only_miss; startNodeRuntimeMetrics adds event-loop and heap metrics; the index lookup logs one 'index/url_lookup' record with timings for maxAge, cache, db and full path.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's edge exposes no /metrics (exporter is inert); wiring the existing metrics crate and adopting 'one canonical log line with outcome and phase timings' per scrape would give the missing run-level observability.

name: Rust native module logs captured and re-emitted into the app logger
what: Logs emitted inside the Rust native code (PDF, HTML, crawler) are collected per call with scrape id and URL context and returned to Node, which re-emits them through the main logger with a 'native' source; on errors the logs are embedded in the error message and extracted on the JS side.
how: with_native_tracing runs a closure under a tracing subscriber, returning logs; process_pdf attaches logs to its result or embed_logs_in_error appends a '__native_logs__:' JSON suffix; emitNativeLogs and extractAndEmitNativeLogs map entries to logger levels with rustTarget and fields.
verevonRelevance: Useful if Verevon embeds Rust transforms in Go or Node hosts; Quarry is pure Rust so tracing spans already flow, but its Go orchestrator could use the same correlation pattern.

name: OpenTelemetry spans across the whole scrape pipeline with LLM traces
what: Spans cover the pipeline (scrape.pipeline, engine loop, robots check, native PDF detect/process, fire-engine calls, index lookups, NuQ operations) with attributes for engine winner, engines attempted, fallback list, unsupported features, cache state and error type; LLM calls are traced through the AI SDK and LangSmith with team, scrape and function ids.
how: withSpan and setSpanAttributes helpers; scrape.pipeline sets scrape.id, url, team, crawl id, features, force_engine, final status, proxy_used, cache_state; engine.fire-engine.perform_scrape records poll count, duration and job id; AI SDK experimental_telemetry carries teamId, functionId, scrapeId, extractId; monitor judge calls and interact runs are traced; ZDR disables all of it.
verevonRelevance: Quarry sets OTLP only when configured; adopting the attribute vocabulary (engine.winner, engines_attempted, unsupported_features, cache_state) would make driver decisions visible in traces and the receipts timeline.

name: Per-request cost tracking with a hard cap and model price table
what: Every LLM call in a scrape adds a record (model, tokens, cost, call-site stack) to a request-scoped tracker that can abort the request when a cost limit is exceeded, and cost is attributed to team and feature through provider labels.
how: CostTracking.addCall pushes {type, metadata, cost, model, tokens, stack}, sums with NaN-proofing and throws CostLimitExceededError when a limit is set; calculateCost uses a per-million-token table (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-5 family, gemini flash, grok, deepseek) with fallback to a model-prices file; withUsageTelemetry wraps every model; Vertex/Google labels carry teamId, functionId, extractId, scrapeId; x-twitter adds per-post search fees.
verevonRelevance: Quarry never enforces max_cost_usd on the step path; a request-scoped tracker with a throwing limit (and call-site stacks for debugging) is the small primitive to enforce it uniformly across Model Plane calls.

name: Per-organisation SIEM audit export with bounded broker and retry ladder
what: Enterprise orgs can stream scrape activity (who, which URL and domain, result, threat decision, ZDR flag, caller-supplied audit username) to Azure Sentinel; delivery is batched per org and gzip-compressed, survives destination outages for about 36 minutes, and is bounded so an outage cannot exhaust memory.
how: buildScrapeActivityEvent produces schema_version 1 events (result success/failure/blocked/cancelled); RabbitMQ transport with a confirm channel, x-max-length 100,000 drop-head, prefetch with per-org batches of 200 or 1 s linger, fixed-delay retry queues 5 s, 30 s, 5 min, 30 min then a DLQ with 7-day retention, Retry-After honoured; per-org config stored encrypted with the destination restricted to credential-free *.ingest.monitor.azure.com HTTPS endpoints; a test endpoint and an ARM deployment template (DCR, connector definition) ship in apps/siem.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Control Plane owns audit; a per-org SIEM exporter for browser and scrape activity (with an allowlisted destination host and bounded delivery) would be a strong enterprise feature that Quarry's receipts and event history could feed.
notes: Quality 5: engineering notes explain why RabbitMQ rather than a Redis queue (bounded backlog, real batching). Introduced 2026-07-27 (git 28c8d3020, #4122).

name: Engine A/B shadow traffic: sampled mirroring or splitting to a staging engine
what: A fraction of non-ZDR scrapes is replayed against a staging API or fire-engine and the outputs are compared asynchronously, so engine changes can be validated on real traffic without affecting customers.
how: abTestJob sends a sampled POST to SCRAPEURL_AB_HOST/v2/scrape (rate SCRAPEURL_AB_RATE, skipped for ZDR and agent jobs); abTestFireEngine returns none, mirror (a promise whose result is compared by scheduleABComparison with timing and status) or split (use another base URL) based on FIRE_ENGINE_AB_URL and rate.
verevonRelevance: Pairs with Quarry's lab/evals: shadow-run a candidate driver or readability change on a sample of tenant-consented, non-ZDR scrapes and diff markdown similarity before rollout.
notes: Earlier Verevon notes call this 'a flag on each scrape'; it is sampling at job and fire-engine level.

name: Quality evaluation: PR-triggered scrape evals and a post-deploy production benchmark
what: Scrape quality and OCR quality are evaluated by an external repository triggered from PRs by hashtag (org members only), and a benchmark run against production starts automatically after each image deploy.
how: scrape-evals.yml dispatches firecrawl-pr-eval repository events with PR, branch and SHA when the PR title/body/comment contains #scrape-quality-eval or #scrape-ocr-eval and the actor is an org member; eval-prod.yml waits 2 minutes after 'Deploy Images to GHCR' succeeds and POSTs eval_run.py with label prod.<sha> to an experiment endpoint.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's SCOREBOARD is '_pending_' for every suite; the cheap fix is the same CI hook: run lab/evals on a labelled PR and after deploy, labelled with the commit SHA.
notes: The evaluation corpus and metrics live in a separate repo (not inspected). Older load-test reports (2024-era, Fly.io machines, Artillery) are in apps/test-suite and are historical.

name: Deterministic HTTP mock record and replay for scraping tests
what: Tests can record every outbound request/response (including fire-engine calls) to JSON and replay them by name through a scrape option, so the engine waterfall is testable without live sites or fire-engine.
how: FIRECRAWL_SAVE_MOCKS makes saveMock write {time, options, result}; loadMock(name) validates the path stays inside the mocks directory; robustFetch and the fetch engine consume matching requests in order; with fire-engine unavailable and a mock present the CDP engines are added to the waterfall; useMock is a scrape option; collect-mocks.js helps gather recordings.
verevonRelevance: Gives Quarry's browser benchmark a deterministic offline mode: record driver-level HTTP and CDP exchanges once and replay for regression tests of escalation logic.
notes: Path traversal in mock names is explicitly guarded.
