name: Hermetic test website, end-to-end 'snips' and a self-host CI matrix
what: Behaviour is tested end to end against a local Astro site (product, branding, robots, prompt-injection pages) through the real API, with tests gated by environment (self-hosted, AI available), and CI runs a matrix of engine, proxy and queue backend combinations.
how: apps/test-site pages; vitest 'snips' under __tests__/snips (v0/v1/v2: crawl, robots, parse, safe-mode, threat-protection, zdr, index-cache variants, browser, monitor, prompt injection, billing); describeIf/HAS_AI/TEST_SUITE_SELF_HOSTED gates; idmux allocates test identities with concurrency and credits; test-server.yml runs engine [playwright, fetch] x proxy [proxy, no-proxy] with searxng, OpenAI and a separate FDB queue job against redis and rabbitmq services; knip dead-code gate; 373 test files in apps/api/src.
verevonRelevance: The strongest process takeaway for Quarry: a controlled local target site with robots, redirect, bot-wall, PDF and prompt-injection pages plus compose-based matrix CI turns the dormant lab/evals into a regression suite.
notes: Quality 5: AGENTS.md mandates a happy-path and failure-path E2E for every API change.

name: Self-host stack: hardened compose, no persistence, unauthenticated by default
what: Docker Compose runs API+workers, a Playwright service, Redis, RabbitMQ, Postgres (NuQ) and optional FoundationDB; the browser container drops all capabilities with no-new-privileges and a noexec tmpfs and has CPU and memory limits, but the stack ships without auth and without persistent volumes.
how: docker-compose.yaml: playwright-service with security_opt no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, cpus 2, mem 4G, tmpfs /tmp/.cache noexec,nosuid; api cpus 4 mem 8G, ulimits nofile 65535, command node dist/src/harness.js --start-docker; health checks for rabbitmq and postgres; logging rotation; env passthrough for model providers (OPENAI_BASE_URL, OLLAMA_BASE_URL, MODEL_NAME), PROXY_*, SEARXNG_*; SELF_HOST.md states the default API is unauthenticated and compose defines no persistent volumes for Postgres, Redis or RabbitMQ; Kubernetes manifests and a Helm chart are provided as starting points.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's compose already refuses ephemeral stores in production; copy the browser container hardening (cap_drop, no-new-privileges, noexec tmpfs, resource limits) for the Chromium host.
notes: Honest docs but not production-ready by design.

name: Polyglot image build with verified artifacts and build SHA stamping
what: One image combines a Go c-shared library, a Rust napi module and the Node app via multi-stage builds, then verifies key output files exist and are non-empty and stamps the git SHA into the runtime.
how: api/Dockerfile stages: golang build of libhtml-to-markdown.so, a Node build stage that installs Rust, FoundationDB client libs and runs pnpm install (which builds the native crate with cache mounts), pnpm prune --prod, a runtime stage copying node_modules, dist, native and the .so, with test -s checks on dist/src/harness.js and others and BUILD_SHA / FIRECRAWL_BUILD_SHA; the Playwright image runs as the node user; CI jobs for npm audit with automated remediation.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's Dockerfile.edge pins Chromium already; the artifact-verification and SHA stamping (surfaced at /version) are cheap guards against shipping a half-built image.

name: Postgres operations as code: tuned WAL, scheduled concurrent reindex, watchdog
what: The queue database ships with its own operational runbook as SQL: checkpoint and WAL settings, aggressive autovacuum for hot tables, staggered REINDEX CONCURRENTLY per index in a low-traffic window, a watchdog that cancels runaway reindexes, and pruning of pg_cron history.
how: nuq.sql sets checkpoint_completion_target, max_wal_size 16 GB, bgwriter and wal_writer settings; per-index cron jobs at 20-minute slots; nuq_maintenance_watchdog every minute cancels REINDEX older than 18 minutes (statement_timeout cannot be set inside a single-statement cron body); cron_job_run_details pruned hourly; comments record measured costs and why each index exists.
verevonRelevance: If Quarry's Postgres queue and event history grow, the same practice (maintenance as migrations, watchdogs) belongs in its deploy/compose Postgres image.

name: Admin plane behind a path secret with queue UI, metrics and cache controls
what: Operators reach a queue dashboard, Prometheus metrics, health probes of dependencies, crawl monitoring, precrawl triggers and cache-clearing endpoints under an unguessable path prefix.
how: index.ts mounts bull-board at /admin/<BULL_AUTH_KEY>/queues only when the key is set (otherwise a warning says admin routes are disabled); admin routes cover redis-health, autumn-health, feng-check, index-queue-prometheus, nuq-metrics, nuq-fdb-metrics, concurrency-queue-backfill, crawl-monitor, precrawl and ACUC/IP/key restriction cache clears, plus partner provisioning proxies.
verevonRelevance: Avoid for Verevon: secret-in-path admin access has no identity or audit; Quarry's HMAC-internal control plus JWT edge is the better pattern, with operator actions logged to Control Plane audit.
notes: Quality 2: workable but weak authentication model.

name: HTTP surface hardening gaps: open CORS, large JSON body and secret-keyed admin
what: The API enables CORS for all origins with defaults, accepts 10 MB JSON bodies and exposes admin routes by path secret; request body bytes are captured for signature verification of inbound integrations (Slack).
how: app.use(cors()) with no options; bodyParser.json({limit:'10mb', verify: captureRawBody}); express-ws for crawl status sockets; trust proxy configurable; x-powered-by disabled; a notFound handler and zod error mapping that rewrites unrecognised-key errors into one message.
verevonRelevance: Checklist item: Verevon's gateway/BFF already normalises headers; ensure Quarry edge never adds permissive CORS and keeps body limits per route.
notes: API keys in headers make permissive CORS less dangerous than cookies would; still unusual for admin surfaces.

name: Hosted-browser security hygiene: opaque upstream errors and validated recording playlists
what: Errors from the browser service are replaced by generic messages because creation failures can contain capability URLs, and session recordings are served only after the HLS playlist is validated (size cap, same-origin segments, well-formed durations).
how: hangar.request converts non-OK upstream responses to HangarError with fixed messages and cancels the body; getHangarRecording fetches the playlist with redirect: error, limits it to 8 MB, requires #EXTM3U, validates #EXTINF pairing, requires every segment URL to share the playlist origin and sums duration.
verevonRelevance: Applies to any Verevon feature proxying provider live-view or replay URLs: never forward upstream bodies, and validate media manifests before relaying them to the browser.

name: Browser session billing: reserve, settle once under a row lock, reconcile unsettled sessions
what: Creating a hosted browser checks credits and reserves a concurrency slot and estimated cost; on stop the actual duration is billed exactly once, with different hourly rates for plain browsing, AI-prompted interaction and ZDR, and a reconciliation pass settles sessions whose stop was missed.
how: createBrowserSession checks credits via Autumn (402), reserveExternalSlot shares the team's scrape concurrency (429), logs the request, inserts browser_sessions; failures stop the browser, release the slot and refund; settleBrowserSessionOnce locks the row, computes credits from created_at/ended_at and rates (120 credits per hour browser, 420 with a prompt, +120 for ZDR, minimum ceil(rate/60)); listUnsettledHangarSessions drives reconciliation; profile save timestamps are recorded.
verevonRelevance: Template for metering Verevon browser grants: reserve at lease creation, settle once from authoritative start/stop times, price AI-driven use higher than human use and reconcile orphaned leases.

name: Entitlement cache that fails open with a short TTL
what: The per-key credit and limits chunk is cached in Redis for 10 minutes under a lock, and when the entitlement service is unreachable the request proceeds with generous default limits cached for only 60 seconds rather than blocking real customers.
how: getACUC reads acuc_<purpose>_<key>_<scrape|extract> from Redis, falls back to a replica query, builds limits through readTeamLimits (Autumn) with FAIL_OPEN_LIMITS and ACUC_FAIL_OPEN_TTL_SECONDS 60, writes with redlock; paid provider calls fail closed instead.
verevonRelevance: Decide explicitly where Quarry fails open (limits lookup) versus closed (billing, ZDR, grants) when Control Plane is unreachable.

name: Tiered PDF pipeline: native classification and extraction, then OCR services, then text fallback
what: A PDF is first classified natively (text-based, scanned, image-based or mixed, with a confidence score and a complexity flag). Clean text PDFs are converted to markdown in Rust without any external service; anything else goes to the FirePDF OCR/layout service, then MinerU on RunPod, and finally a plain text extractor.
how: processPdf (Rust pdf-inspector, run on the tokio blocking pool) returns pdfType, confidence, isComplex, pagesNeedingOcr, title and markdown; getIneligibleReason accepts only TextBased with confidence >= 0.95 and no complex layout; mode 'fast' throws PDFOCRRequiredError for scanned or image-based files; otherwise FirePDF is used (sampled by FIRE_PDF_PERCENT, default 10, or forced for pages/blocks/markers), on failure RunPod MinerU for files under 19 MB, on failure pdf-parse. Page count and title come from native detection; truncation is reported via numPages versus totalPages.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's PDF text path uses lopdf only on the answer pipeline; a classify-then-route design (cheap native path for clean text, OCR provider only when needed) would give scrape and ingest real PDF coverage without sending every file to an OCR vendor.
notes: Quality 5: cost-aware routing with fail-down chain. FirePDF and MinerU are external; only their clients are in the repo.

name: PDF parser options: modes, page limits, per-page markdown, typed blocks, page markers, refresh
what: Callers choose how PDFs are parsed: fast (native only, fail on scans), auto, or ocr; cap the pages; request per-page markdown, typed layout blocks with bounding boxes and reading order, or page markers between pages; or refresh a cached conversion.
how: parsers default to ['pdf','image']; pdfParserWithOptions {mode, maxPages, pages (alias pageMarkdown), blocks, pageMarkers, refresh, __firePdfAsync}; blocks carry id, type, label, bbox, content, markdownSpan, readingOrder, source and layout/OCR confidence; options that need FirePDF throw if it is not configured; truncated parses are never cached; maxPages and numPages/totalPages expose truncation.
verevonRelevance: Typed blocks with bbox and reading order are what a Verevon document viewer or citation UI needs to highlight sources; Data Plane chunking could consume them as SourceTrace anchors.

name: Large-PDF async processing by reference with in-flight job adoption and non-cancelling timeouts
what: Big PDFs are not sent inline: the file is uploaded (or its handoff reference reused) and an asynchronous OCR job is polled. A second request for the same document adopts the job already running, abandoned jobs are deliberately left to finish, and a timeout tells the caller that processing continues and when to retry.
how: FirePDF async client: submitJob, pollUntilTerminal, fetchResult, cancelJob (2 s timeout, DELETE /jobs/<scrapeId>); by-reference flow checks a raw-sha256 content cache before uploading 30-256 MB, can server-side copy a fire-engine GCS handoff object, or adopts an existing job found by content lookup (adoptScrapeId); deadlines are computed per page (1.25 s/page plus 60 s base) and surfaced as processing_continues details with Retry-After; ZDR traffic is excluded because the input object persists; async routing is a server-controlled cohort (percentage, forced/disabled team ids, bulk-origin percentage).
verevonRelevance: Applicable to any long Quarry or Model Plane job that outlives a request: content-addressed dedupe of in-flight work, honest 'still processing' semantics and retry hints beat blind retries.
notes: Quality 5: unusually careful lifecycle reasoning documented in comments. Async FirePDF client added 2026-05-14 (git 63eeeedd0, #3526).

name: Content-addressed PDF result cache with variants and a fail-closed refresh budget
what: Parsed PDFs are cached by the hash of their bytes, with separate variants for page-aware and block-aware results; callers can force a re-parse but only within a small per-team token budget, and when the budget is exhausted the cached result is served.
how: createPdfCacheKey = sha256 of the payload (or 'raw-<sha256>' for by-reference), entries stored in GCS under provider prefixes with markdown, html, pagesProcessed, pageMarkdown, blocks, provenance and cachedAt; FIRE_PDF_CACHE_REFRESH_PER_MINUTE (default 10) rate-limits refresh via rate-limiter-flexible and remembers one decision per scrape id so fallback engines do not spend another token; a cache service can be asked with both keyspaces.
verevonRelevance: Hash-keyed document caches are ZDR-safe in a way URL-keyed caches are not (the key reveals nothing about the source) provided the stored text itself is org-scoped; relevant to Data Plane ingest dedupe.
notes: Cache is global across teams in the cloud product; org scoping would be required for Verevon.

name: Resource governance around parsers: extraction semaphore, size ceilings, per-page time budget, shadow comparison
what: Native PDF extraction is bounded to a few concurrent jobs per process so bursts cannot exhaust memory, files have per-path size ceilings (19 MB MinerU, 30 MB inline FirePDF, 50 MB raw, 256 MB by reference), PDFs that cannot finish within the remaining timeout fail early with a specific error, and Rust output is silently compared with OCR output to measure quality.
how: withPdfExtractionPermit around processPdf/detectPdf (PDF_EXTRACTION_CONCURRENCY default 3, FIFO with wait/hold histograms), constants in pdf/types.ts, PDFInsufficientTimeError when pages x 150 ms exceeds the remaining timeout, comparePdfOutputs logged asynchronously with URL omitted for ZDR; MAX_GUNZIPPED_FILE_SIZE for browser handoffs.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's transform crates run in-process on the edge; a bounded permit for heavy parsers and typed 'insufficient time' failures prevent head-of-line blocking of the scrape fast path.
notes: The semaphore comment records the production OOM that motivated it.

name: Office and e-book conversion in Rust with decompression budgets
what: DOCX, DOC, XLSX, PPTX, ODT/ODS/ODP, RTF, CSV, EPUB and more are converted to GitHub-flavoured markdown natively, with DOCX headers and footers added, and OOXML archives are read under strict byte and part budgets to resist zip bombs.
how: convert_document_to_markdown (anydoc 0.2.2) detects the format from bytes with an extension hint; for DOCX it parses _rels and header/footer parts with roxmltree under ZipReadBudget (128 MB total and per part, 256 parts, 256 header/footer references); the Node document engine wraps it, converts markdown to HTML, and routes through the same handoff and prefetch logic as PDFs; formats are listed by /v2/parse/formats.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's docx.rs is unwired and XLSX/PPTX/EPUB are absent; a native converter with archive budgets can be adopted behind Quarry's content-type router and reused by the Data Plane ingest path.
notes: The scrapeURL README still describes LlamaParse and mammoth; code is ground truth.

name: Main-content extraction in a streaming Rust transform with lazy-image resolution
what: HTML is cleaned natively: head, meta, style, script and noscript are removed, include/exclude selectors applied, 42 non-main selectors (header, footer, nav, sidebar, modals, ads, cookie banners...) stripped unless they contain a force-include region, lazy-loaded images resolved from srcset or data-src to the largest source, and all links and image URLs made absolute.
how: transform_html in html.rs (kuchikiki DOM) with EXCLUDE_NON_MAIN_TAGS and FORCE_INCLUDE_MAIN_TAGS, base-href aware URL resolution, srcset parsing choosing the largest width/density, data-srcset/data-src fallback; wrapped in spawn_blocking; TS falls back to cheerio when the native call fails; onlyMainContent defaults true.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's readability subset strips images and landmarks; the lazy-image resolution and force-include escape hatch are small, testable improvements for its html2md path.
notes: Quality 3: heuristic selector lists (including site-specific swoogo classes) rather than a scored content model.

name: Learned domain boilerplate signatures (OMCE) applied before main-content selectors
what: For indexed domains, repeated page chrome is learned across many pages and removed by structural signature before the static selector pass, so templates that selectors miss are still stripped.
how: When __experimental_omce is set, htmlTransform fetches signatures for the domain (query_omce_signatures) and passes omce_signatures to the Rust transform, which computes node signatures per mode (external nodesig crate) bottom-up and detaches elements whose signature is in the learned set; sendDocumentToIndex enqueues OMCE jobs per domain level via Redis and insert_omce_job_if_needed; the signature learning job itself and the nodesig algorithm are not in this repo.
verevonRelevance: A genuinely different approach to boilerplate removal: learn per-site templates from the corpus of pages Quarry already scrapes (tracked sources, snapshots) and apply them as a pre-pass; fits Quarry's persisted HTML artifacts.
notes: Medium confidence: the meaning of OMCE is inferred from usage (domain-level signatures consumed by the transform); marked experimental in the request schema.

name: HTML to Markdown in three tiers: Go service, in-process Go library, turndown fallback
what: Markdown conversion prefers a separate Go HTTP service (to keep the Node event loop free), then an in-process Go shared library over FFI, then a JavaScript turndown fallback, followed by a Rust post-processing pass.
how: parseMarkdown tries convertHTMLToMarkdownWithHttpService when HTML_TO_MARKDOWN_SERVICE_URL is set (axios, X-Request-ID and X-Zero-Data-Retention headers, 150 MB body limit in the service), then koffi-loaded ConvertHTMLToMarkdown from libhtml-to-markdown.so (USE_GO_MARKDOWN_PARSER), then turndown with the joplin GFM plugin; every path runs postProcessMarkdown (native) which also fixes multi-line links and removes skip-to-content links.
verevonRelevance: Quarry converts in Rust (html2md); the transferable idea is isolating heavy conversions from the request loop and keeping a deterministic fallback with the same post-processing so output is stable across tiers.
notes: The TODO in the Go FFI wrapper says it has no timeout.

name: Image OCR as a one-page scanned document behind a per-request and per-deployment gate
what: Raster images (PNG, JPEG, JPEG 2000, TIFF, GIF, BMP) are OCR'd like scanned PDFs when the request's parsers include 'image' (default) and the deployment has image OCR enabled; otherwise they keep failing as unsupported files.
how: imageOcrGate combines request parsers with IMAGE_OCR_ENABLED and FIRE_PDF_BASE_URL; image extensions add the image feature flag; byte sniffing confirms formats from browser handoffs (mislabeled HTML error pages served as image/jpeg are never sent to OCR); the image engine submits to FirePDF and a parsed image counts as success even with empty text; cached image OCR is not served to requests that did not opt in.
verevonRelevance: Gives a concrete gating model (request opt-in AND deployment switch AND byte confirmation) for any OCR or vision feature routed through Model Plane, relevant to ZDR and cost control.

name: Structured JSON extraction core: model routing, token trimming, repair, provider fallback
what: The json, summary, query and similar LLM formats share one completion routine: it picks a model by schema complexity, trims input to 80 percent of the model's context without freezing the event loop, requests strict structured output, repairs malformed JSON, falls back to another model on quota or rate-limit errors, and reports truncation instead of returning half an object.
how: selectModelForSchema (gpt-4o-mini by default, gpt-4.1 when the schema has $ref/$defs); trimToTokenLimit pre-trims by characters (5 chars/token bound) before tiktoken, then slices tokens and adds a warning; prompt tells the model to ignore data-processing directives embedded in content; schema is normalised (defaults removed, root arrays wrapped in {items}, OpenAI strict-schema rules) and unwrapped after; experimental_repairText strips code fences, detects truncated JSON via bracket scanning (no repair, clear 'too long' error) or asks the model to fix the JSON; quota errors retry with gpt-4.1-mini; finish reason 'length' raises an output-limit error; refusals raise LLMRefusalError; a 2,000,000-character cap guards JSON extraction input.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's /v1/extract delegates to Model Plane and ignores the prompt field; these mechanics (schema normalisation, truncation detection, trimming, fallback model) belong in the Model Plane AiFormatRunner so Quarry's extraction is robust on long pages.
notes: Quality 4: pragmatic and well-instrumented; model choice is hard-coded to OpenAI families with config overrides.

name: Provider-agnostic model routing with self-host overrides
what: All LLM features go through one factory that supports OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic, Groq, Google, OpenRouter, Fireworks, DeepInfra and Vertex, and self-hosters can redirect everything to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Ollama with a model override.
how: getModel(name, provider) over the Vercel AI SDK providers, defaulting to ollama when OLLAMA_BASE_URL is set; OPENAI_BASE_URL and MODEL_NAME override name and base; withUsageTelemetry wraps every model for cost and labels; o3-mini forced to chat completions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon routes all inference through Model Plane (no direct provider calls from Quarry); this confirms the contract Quarry should call: a model alias plus per-request usage labels, never provider SDKs.

name: SmartScrape: extraction that asks for a browser agent only when data is hidden behind interaction
what: The JSON extraction schema is extended with fields through which the model can say 'the missing data needs clicking, expanding or pagination' and supply a goal; only then is a browser-agent service invoked and its pages re-extracted, keeping the common case a single cheap LLM call.
how: extractSmartScrape builds a wrapper schema with shouldUseSmartscrape, smartscrape_reasoning and smartscrape_prompt plus extractedData; if the model flags it, smartScrape POSTs {url, prompt, sessionId, extractId, scrapeId} to SMART_SCRAPE_API_URL/smart-scrape and receives scrapedPages (html, reason, page) and token usage, which are checked by the prompt-injection guard and merged; costs are tracked against the request limit.
verevonRelevance: A cost-ordered escalation path for Verevon: static scrape, LLM extract, and only then a governed browser run proposed by the model and executed or rejected by Quarry, matching the plane rule that Model proposes and Quarry executes.
notes: The smart-scrape service is closed.

name: deterministicJson: LLM-generated extractor code, run in a sandbox, cached and cheap to reuse
what: Instead of calling an LLM on every page, the model writes a small DOM extractor for a (URL, schema, prompt) once; later scrapes run the cached code in a sandbox, optionally calling back to the model for sub-questions, with selector self-repair when selectors prove too strict.
how: extractDeterministicJson keys the extractor by sha256(CACHE_VERSION, CODEGEN_MODEL, url, schema, prompt) in Postgres tables deterministic_json_scripts and deterministic_json_llm_cache; generate builds anchor HTML context and asks the model for code (static validation of shape and globals); runExtractorInSandbox sends code, html and url over WebSocket to CODE_SANDBOX_URL with a host RPC channel 'askLlm' (bounded by maxAskLlmCalls); tooStrictSelectors triggers one regeneration with feedback; output is parsed against the JSON schema; billed 10 credits on generation and 3 on reuse.
verevonRelevance: Strong fit for Quarry's planned site profiles and adaptive target memory: compile a reusable extractor per site template and run it with no model cost; the sandbox host-call channel is a safe way to let generated code ask bounded questions.
notes: Cache key includes the exact URL so reuse is per page, not per template (INF from the key composition). Introduced 2026-06-04 (git ef56b5ce4, #3706).

name: Change tracking: whitespace-insensitive comparison, git-style and LLM JSON diffs, tag grouping
what: The changeTracking format compares the current markdown with the previous scrape of the same URL and tag and reports new, same, changed or removed; optional git-style unified diff and an LLM-produced or schema-based JSON diff are available. It is unsupported under zero data retention.
how: deriveDiff loads the last scrape via the change-tracking store (Bigtable row pointing to a stored job document), normalises both markdown strings by removing whitespace and iframe links then sorts characters to compare, marks 404 as removed, builds createMarkdownChangeDiff for git-diff mode, and for json mode either extracts a schema from both versions and compares keys or asks the model to summarise differences; visibility 'hidden' for URLs not in the current crawl.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's change detection is a raw blake3 compare with an unwired paragraph differ; the whitespace/order-insensitive normalisation plus tag-scoped baselines would remove most false positives immediately.
notes: Quality 3: sorting characters makes the comparison a multiset check, which can miss reorderings; the doc comment says bag-of-characters is the intent for noise tolerance (INF).

name: Goal-aware LLM judge for monitor changes with fail-open alerts
what: Monitors can alert only on changes that matter to a stated goal: a model reads the diff and the goal, decides whether the change is meaningful, lists the exact added/removed/changed items with before and after text, and defaults to 'meaningful' whenever the judge fails.
how: judgeChange sends MONITOR GOAL, optional extraction prompt, unified markdown diff and field diffs to gemini-3.5-flash (temperature 0, 30 s timeout, 3 attempts with jittered backoff), strict JSON {meaningful, confidence, reason, meaningfulChanges[]} with rules treating page content as untrusted data and ignoring counters, timestamps and rotating blocks unless the goal asks; sanitiseMeaningfulChanges validates shape; alertMode first_match, every_new_result or material_dev; calls are traced and not recorded under ZDR.
verevonRelevance: Directly addresses Quarry's noise problem (every dynamic token is a 'change'); a Model Plane judge with an explicit goal and fail-open default fits the alerting path to notification-core.
notes: Verbatim before/after evidence is requested in the prompt but not verified in code; validation is structural only.

name: Field-level PII redaction transform that fails closed
what: redactPII replaces people, emails, phones, locations, financial data and secrets in the returned markdown by tags, masks or removal, with accurate, aggressive and fast modes; if redaction fails or the page is too large, the markdown is returned empty rather than leaking raw text.
how: performRedactPII calls a separate fire-privacy service (model, Presidio and spaCy recognisers per mode; documented precision/recall tradeoffs) after markdown derivation and before later transformers; options {mode, entities, replaceStyle}; +4 credits per page and +4 per extra PDF page; the cache still stores raw HTML (see cache write policy).
verevonRelevance: A Data Plane or Model Plane redaction step before ingest/answer is consistent with Verevon's privacy posture; fail-closed-on-error and pipeline placement (after markdown, before LLM formats) are the design points.
notes: The redaction service is closed; the 'raw HTML cached' observation is INF from write conditions.

name: LLM prompt-injection guard for scraped content with chunking and fail-open billing
what: An opt-in check (checkPromptInjection) classifies the scraped page with a model before it is handed to extraction or agents, and aborts the scrape with a typed error when the page tries to steer an AI. The classifier is told page content is untrusted, uses a randomised delimiter, and distinguishes attacks by whether the AI would have the capability to act, not by politeness.
how: checkForPromptInjection splits markdown into 32,000-character chunks with 2,000 overlap, scans batches of 5 concurrently through a semaphore with gpt-4o-mini and a strict boolean+reason schema, wraps each chunk in <untrusted_page_content_UUID> tags, aborts on any 'injection' verdict (PromptInjectionDetectedError) and fails open on classifier errors; the fee (+4 credits, 5 credits for a blocked failure) is charged only when every chunk got a verdict; the extraction prompt additionally tells the model to ignore embedded directives; the same guard runs on smart-scrape pages; a test site page and a snips test exercise it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's browser observations have no injection labelling or detection (design only in the automation improvements doc, section 20); a guard on page text entering Model Plane prompts, with randomised delimiters and capability-based criteria, is the most concrete reference available.
notes: Fail-open is a policy choice that Verevon should likely invert for high-risk actions. Detection is model-based, so bypass is possible; it complements, not replaces, approval gates. Introduced 2026-08-26 (git ac154d26c, #4392).

name: Interact agent: accessibility-tree refs through the agent-browser CLI inside the sandbox, with guardrails
what: The prompt-driven interact mode runs an LLM that drives the hosted browser by issuing agent-browser CLI commands (snapshot with interactive @eN refs, click, fill, type, select, check, press, hover, scroll, wait, find by role/text/placeholder, frame, eval, back) through the sandbox's bash execution; it is capped at 25 steps, may not open new tabs, and is shown an action log before every step.
how: executePromptViaBrowserAgent selects the visible tab through a CDP snippet, takes an initial 'agent-browser snapshot -i' (capped at 40,000 characters) and current URL, runs generateText with a single 'browser' tool and stopWhen stepCountIs(25), blocks commands matching 'tab new' or 'open', re-selects the tab after each command, and injects an ACTION LOG with common-mistake hints (forgot Enter, stale refs, no re-snapshot) in prepareStep; ZDR runs use a different model with store=false and no LangSmith tracing; debug logs are written only outside production and never for ZDR.
verevonRelevance: Corrects the earlier inventory ('no accessibility snapshot'): Firecrawl's agent does use @ref snapshots, but through an external CLI in the sandbox rather than in this repo. Verevon's @eN refs bound to CDP backend ids with fail-closed repair are stronger; the step-cap, tab lock and action-log hints are cheap additions to Model Plane's planner.
notes: In Verevon's architecture this loop would live in Model Plane, not Quarry.

name: Domain-matched provider tools returned with a scrape, and idempotent paid provider execution
what: A scrape or search can return provider tools matched to the page's domain or query ('domainTools'); provider calls then run through scrape/search with a metered flow (authorise, quote, reserve, execute, settle) that is idempotent per request id and fails closed when entitlement or plan cannot be verified.
how: services/alexandria: discovery is free and returns contracts in data.tools; execution authorises against the org's data-source access flags and provider terms, quotes, reserves credits with a lock id alexandria_<chargeId>, executes with budget and deadline headers, finalises the receipt, enqueues a ledger write and a usage event; charge id = sha256(teamId, x-request-id) with a 7-day Redis record whose states are completed (replay), same id different payload (409), in flight (409), refused (record dropped) or unresolved (503, kept for manual reconciliation); caller Authorization is forwarded only on execution.
verevonRelevance: The closest Firecrawl analogue to integration-corev2 actions: a URL's domain should suggest connector actions (GitHub URL to github actions), and the idempotency states table is a model for Verevon's write attestations and billing events.
notes: Mostly from the service README; paid settlement is stated to be covered by mocked tests only. Upstream exchange service is closed.

name: Signed outbound webhooks with SSRF checks, event filters, optional broker queue and delivery logs
what: Job events (crawl, batch, extract, monitor, agent) can be pushed to a customer URL with an HMAC-SHA256 signature; targets resolving to private addresses are refused, event names can be filtered with wildcards, delivery can be moved to a RabbitMQ queue, and every attempt is logged.
how: WebhookSender.send builds {success, type, id|jobId, webhookId uuid, data, error, metadata}, signs the body into X-Firecrawl-Signature: sha256=<hmac>, posts with the cookie-less secure dispatcher and a 10 s timeout (30 s for v0), skips events not matching configured names (full name, suffix or legacy sub-type), publishes to a persistent 'webhooks' queue when WEBHOOK_USE_RABBITMQ is set, and appends outcomes to a Redis list batch-inserted into webhook_logs; the direct path has a single attempt and no retry.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's control dispatcher already has HMAC, backoff (1 s to 1 h), 5 attempts and a DLQ, which beats this; the missing Verevon pieces are tenant scoping and edge exposure, plus the wildcard event filter.
notes: Retry and replay of failed webhooks is not visible in this repo.

name: Credit pricing that follows cost drivers: failures free, LLM features surcharged, reuse discounted
what: A page costs 1 credit; json extraction, PII redaction, lockdown and the prompt-injection check add 4 each, URL threat scans add 2, PDF pages cost 1 each, a generated deterministic extractor costs 10 and a reused one 3; failed scrapes cost nothing except guard/scan work already done; hosted browser time is billed per hour with higher rates for AI-driven use and ZDR.
how: calculateCreditsToBeBilled adds constants (jsonCostBonus 4, redactPIICostBonus 4, threatScanCost 2, lockdown +4, deterministic 10 vs 3 detected from cost-tracking tags, injection guard +4 only when every chunk got a verdict) and returns only guard and scan fees on failure; browser rates 120/420/+120 credits per hour with a minimum charge; Exchange provider results are priced by the provider; credit locks reserve then settle.
verevonRelevance: Quarry emits usage events (scrape.page, crawl.seed...) with no credit logic; Control Plane could price Quarry features the same way, keyed off the cost tracker, with 'no charge on failure' as a product rule.
notes: Autumn/Firebill (external) hold the ledger; only the calculation is visible.

name: Strict request validation, typed option dependencies and spec drift
what: Scrape requests are validated with strict objects (unknown keys are rejected with a single clear message), cross-field rules (changeTracking needs markdown, one screenshot, rawBase64 alone, waitFor at most half the timeout, profile not with lockdown) and string/format normalisation; hand-maintained OpenAPI files lag the code.
how: scrapeOptionFields uses z.strictObject with refinements, formats union with 20 object types, actions refine (max 50, 60 s wait), URL schema accepting scheme-less URLs and IP literals; the error handler converts unrecognized_keys into 'Unrecognized key in body -- please review the v2 API documentation'; openapi.json omits several formats (audio, video, question, attributes, highlights, summary, images, product, menu, deterministicJson) and the pdf action, and lists proxy default basic while code defaults auto.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's OpenAPI already covers only about 60 percent of routes; generating the spec from the same validators (zod, schemars) avoids Firecrawl's drift.
notes: Quality 3: strong validation, hand-written spec.

name: One background worker multiplexes write-behind batchers and reconcilers
what: Hot-path side effects are written to Redis lists and flushed in batches by a background worker (index inserts, webhook logs, activity updates, billing batches), alongside reconcilers such as a 15-second browser-session reconciliation and the precrawl and engpicker loops.
how: index-worker.ts sets intervals: processIndexInsertJobs (Redis list index-insert-queue, batch 100), processWebhookInsertJobs (batch 1000), processBrowserSessionActivityJobs, reconcileBrowserSessions every 15 s, processOMCEJobs, a billing batch processor, the precrawl queue consumer, the SIEM consumer and an engpicker polling loop; enqueuers only do an RPUSH/SADD so the scrape path never waits on the database; failures are logged and swallowed.
verevonRelevance: Pattern for Quarry's artifact and receipt writes: keep the scrape latency path free of metadata DB writes by batching through a durable list, as long as ZDR rows bypass it and lost items are tolerable.
notes: Redis lists lose items on eviction or restart; acceptable for index and log rows, not for billing-grade data (billing has its own queue).

name: Run history: request/child rows, result blobs, TTL access rows and ZDR-scrubbed records
what: Every API job writes a request row and child rows (scrapes, crawls, searches...), result bodies go to object storage, and a short-lived access row authorises later retrieval; for ZDR requests the stored row keeps outcome and cost but replaces URL, options and cost tracking with redaction markers and schedules deletion.
how: logRequest inserts requests with target_hint, origin, integration and a redaction marker when ZDR, writes ApiJobAccess to Bigtable with expiry (default 24 h, crawlTtlHours for crawls) and enqueues a ZDR cleanup job; logScrape publishes rows via Pub/Sub with sanitised text (NUL bytes dropped, lone surrogates replaced) and nulls url, options, cost_tracking and pdf pages under ZDR; PostHog first-use events are skipped for ZDR; the job log has no Postgres copy since 2026-10-09.
verevonRelevance: A concrete row shape for Quarry run history that satisfies ZDR: keep outcome, timing and cost, redact target and options, schedule deletion; the TTL access row is a clean way to authorise result retrieval without a long-lived registry.
notes: Hosted-only stores (Bigtable, ClickHouse, Pub/Sub) are not self-hostable in this repo.

name: SERP provider fallback chain with ZDR and anonymous search modes
what: Search uses the hosted fire-engine search when configured (with ZDR and anonymous routing modes and enforced include/exclude domains), otherwise a self-hosted SearXNG, otherwise a best-effort DuckDuckGo HTML scrape that rotates 7 static user agents and raises an anti-bot error when the results page shows its anomaly modal; any error returns an empty result.
how: search() in search/v2/index.ts selects by config: FIRE_ENGINE_BETA_URL, SEARXNG_ENDPOINT, then ddgSearch with a 7-entry user-agent list and a DDGAntiBotError triggered by the .anomaly-modal__modal element; includeDomains and excludeDomains are enforced on returned URLs only on the fire-engine path and otherwise appear as a site: chain in the query; enterprise modes default, anon and zdr are passed to the hosted path; the catch-all returns {}.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's router already has Brave, Serper, SearXNG and Stract with ZDR gating; Firecrawl's 'enforce domain filters on results, not just in the query' and the explicit anonymous mode are the details to check against Quarry's include/exclude handling.
notes: Silent empty results on error hide provider outages from callers.

name: Persistent profile registry reconciled with tombstones against the browser service
what: Named browser profiles live in the browser service, while the app keeps a listing; saves only move the listing forward in time and a deletion tombstone prevents a late save from resurrecting a deleted profile.
how: upsertBrowserProfile uses GREATEST(saved_at) and keeps size_bytes from the newest save; deleteHangarProfile returns a deleted_at timestamp which is stored under browser-profile-deleted:<team,name>; deleteBrowserProfile removes only rows whose saved_at is not newer than the deletion; profile names are limited to 128 UTF-8 bytes; session settlement records profile_saved_at; saveChanges (default true) controls whether a session saves its changes back to the profile.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's profile stores (memory/Postgres/Redis, unwired S3) need the same ordering guarantees when two sessions of one profile end near each other; also supports a read-only (saveChanges=false) profile mode.

name: Media extraction through a capability-advertising helper service using browser cookies
what: The audio and video formats download media through a helper service (avgrab) that publishes a regex of URLs it supports; the scrape passes cookies captured from the browser session so consent- or login-gated media can be fetched, and the helper returns a public URL.
how: fetchAudio/fetchVideo cache GET /supported-urls for 5 minutes, reject unsupported URLs with a typed error, POST /download (audio) or /download-video (video) with {url, cookies} and a 240 s timeout, map access-denied errors to a typed MediaAccessDeniedError and set document.audio/video to data.public_url; the chrome-cdp engine adds a getCookies action when audio, video or the YouTube postprocessor will run; lockdown skips the call; avgrab-resolve also resolves post URLs for map.
verevonRelevance: The pattern of helper services that advertise what they can handle (regex or capability list) keeps routing logic out of Quarry; useful for a future transcription or media-capture driver behind Model Plane.
notes: Cookie handoff from browser to helper is a credential-forwarding path that would need explicit approval in Verevon.

name: Resilient internal HTTP client: schema-validated JSON, retry on error or status, no socket timeouts, DNS cache
what: All calls to helper services (fire-engine, FirePDF, smart-scrape, avgrab) go through one client that validates JSON against a zod schema, retries on transport errors and non-2xx statuses with an optional cooldown, never cuts long jobs with socket timeouts (aborts come from the request signal instead), caches DNS lookups, keeps PDF payloads out of logs and supports recorded mocks.
how: robustFetch builds requests with undici fetch on two Agents with headersTimeout 0 and bodyTimeout 0 (cacheable-lookup or plain dns.lookup), retries by recursion with tryCount-1 and tryCooldown, treats status >= 300 as failure unless ignoreFailureStatus, parses JSON then schema.parse with distinct error messages for malformed JSON, schema mismatch and parse failure, redacts file_content and pdf bodies from logged params, and in mock mode matches requests by URL plus method (fire-engine requests additionally by engine and target URL). cacheable-lookup is also installed on the global http and https agents except in dev.
verevonRelevance: The Quarry edge-to-control and edge-to-Model-Plane clients should share one policy for retry, schema validation and mock-ability; note that process-wide DNS caching is a poor fit with a resolve-once-and-pin SSRF design.
notes: The retry loop retries every failure including non-idempotent POSTs (fire-engine submit); idempotency relies on the remote job id.

name: Adaptive wait ( smart wait cache ) flag passed to the hosted browser
what: The hosted browser appears to learn how long pages need to settle and cache it per site; crawls turn this off so page loads stay uniform across a crawl.
how: internalOptions.disableSmartWaitCache is forwarded to fire-engine chrome-cdp requests; v2 crawl sets it to true in the stored crawl internal options; the learning itself is inside closed fire-engine.
verevonRelevance: If Quarry adds hydration-settle heuristics (it has an automatic settle in the browser adapter), per-host learned wait times are the natural next step; treat Firecrawl as an idea source only.
notes: Low confidence: only the flag name and call sites are visible; behaviour is inferred.
